title: Actions to Respond to the Drug Poisoning Crisis in Toronto
topics: community crisis response, health, substance abuse; alcohol abuse; drug abuse; drug addiction, crisis response, health coverage
brief: The status quo approach to the drug poisoning crisis is not working. There is an urgent need for a comprehensive public health approach to drug policy that removes structural barriers to healthcare and social services, provides alternatives to the toxic drug supply, and enhances and expands services to improve the health and well-being of Toronto's communities. Toronto continues to be in the midst of a drug poisoning crisis, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Climate Change and the Role of Public Health
topics: climate change, public health; climate protection
brief: With Toronto set to debate its path to a 2040 Net Zero Climate Action Plan, it is imperative we look to ensure all of the City's efforts are geared toward achieving the targets our plan will set out. The targets included in the City's plan are great, but the City of Toronto lacks the explicit powers to do what is necessary - a full phase out of natural gas in existing and new buildings imminently. The Board of Health is asked to request the Medical Officer of Health to review the potential to declare a public health emergency as it relates to the phasing out of natural gas if the Province of Ontario refuses to implement such policy in the coming year.

brief: In recent years the process of negotiations between the City and developers on applications which have been appealed to the Ontario Land Use Tribunal has been questioned with respect to the degree of public transparency. Further, Council is often put in a position of having to consider a settlement offer with: very little time for review; limited ability to discuss it publicly; and, advice which can appear to the public as different from the advice provided in previous public reports. Planning and Housing Committee is asked to direct the City Solicitor, in consultation with the Chief Planner and the City Clerk to report in the first quarter of 2022 on the negotiation process for development applications which have been appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

Cultural districts are also unique and complex in terms of their character and community resources available. City Council is asked to direct the General Manager, Economic Development and Culture to undertake public engagement on the development of a cultural districts program that strengthens local culture and communities.

brief: The purpose of this report is to recommend the program objectives, guidelines and impact framework for a new Cultural Festivals Funding Program to support and increase the accountability and transparency of City funding to cultural festivals. City Council is asked to approve the establishment of the Cultural Festivals Funding Program, substantially in accordance with the City of Toronto Cultural Festivals Grant Program Guidelines in Attachment 3 to this report, with implementation commencing in 2022.

brief: In February 2020, the Office of the Integrity Commissioner received three complaints about the conduct of then Councillor Jim Karygiannis arising from articles in the Toronto Star dated February 8 and 11, 2020. brief: Councillor Fletcher asks City Council to direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body, with appropriate staff, to oppose the minor variance application for 23 Fielding Avenue. The application sought four variances for a rear two-storey addition, a rear ground floor deck and a rear one-storey detached garage on a two-storey semi-detached dwelling. The Committee of Adjustment had refused the application.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Ted Reeve Community Arena Board
topics: board members;
brief: The City Clerk recommends the Toronto and East York Community Council appoint four candidates to the Ted Reeve Community Arena Board, at pleasure of Council, for terms ending June 25, 2025. The named candidates in the public summary are Michael Appt, Joanne Davidson and Iain McLeod.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 6K to exclude the development located at 177, 183 and 197 Front Street East, and 15-21 Lower Sherbourne Street, and 200 The Esplanade
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to realign Permit Parking Area 6K to exclude the development at 177, 183 and 197 Front Street East, 15-21 Lower Sherbourne Street and 200 The Esplanade, so current permit holders keep enough parking space. Because the TTC operates on those streets, City Council approval is required. Council is asked to approve the revised 6K map in Schedule B of the permit parking by-law.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 4I and the exclusion of the development located at 938-950 King Street West and 95-99 Strachan Avenue
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to realign Permit Parking Area 4I to exclude the development at 938-950 King Street West and 95-99 Strachan Avenue, so current permit holders keep enough parking space. Because the TTC operates on King Street West, City Council approval is required. Council is asked to approve the revised 4I map in Schedule B of the permit parking by-law.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 2 to exclude the development located at 1494-1502 Dundas Street West
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to realign Permit Parking Area 2 to exclude the development at 1494-1502 Dundas Street West, so current permit holders keep enough parking space. Because the TTC operates on Dundas Street West, City Council approval is required. Council is asked to approve the revised map in Schedule B of the permit parking by-law.
address: 1494 Dundas Toronto Ontario; 1502 Dundas Toronto Ontario

title: 73 Queen's Park Crescent East - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: employment opportunities, official plan amendments, public realm, zoning bylaws; careers; employment; job applications; job boards; job openings; job opportunities; job postings; job vacancies; jobs; vacancies (jobs), public spaces, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve an Official Plan and zoning amendment for a five-storey, 7,024-square-metre institutional building at 73 Queen's Park Crescent East. The proposal is described as a compact built form appropriate for intensification in the built-up area.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 2 to exclude the development located at 646-648 Dufferin Street and 1-3 Boland Lane
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to realign Permit Parking Area 2 to exclude the development at 646-648 Dufferin Street and 1-3 Boland Lane, so current permit holders keep enough parking space. Because the TTC operates on Dufferin Street, City Council approval is required. Council is asked to approve the revised map in Schedule B of the permit parking by-law.
address: 1 Boland Toronto Ontario; 3 Boland Toronto Ontario; 646 Dufferin Toronto Ontario; 648 Dufferin Toronto Ontario

title: Traffic Control Signals and Turn Prohibitions - Dufferin Street
topics: traffic control systems; traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council install traffic control signals at Dufferin Street and Lindsey Avenue, and prohibit northbound and southbound right turns on red at all times there. The recommendation follows Council's December 2020 direction to review cyclist and pedestrian safety on Dufferin Street. Because the TTC operates on Dufferin Street, City Council approval is required.

title: Parking Amendments - Davisville Avenue
topics: stopping prohibitions; no stopping
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to prohibit stopping on both sides of Davisville Avenue by Davisville Junior Public School and Spectrum Alternative School, as part of the school board's Traffic Safety Program. The change would discourage pick-up and drop-off activity during school hours. Because the TTC operates on Davisville Avenue, City Council approval is required.
address: 50 Millwood Toronto Ontario; Toronto Ontario Davisville Yonge

title: 316-320 Dupont Street - Zoning Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: zoning;
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve a zoning amendment for a nine-storey office building with ground-floor retail at 316-320 Dupont Street, 48.6 metres including the mechanical penthouse. The building would be integrated with the proposed mixed-use building at 328-332 Dupont Street.
address: 316 Dupont Toronto Ontario; 320 Dupont Toronto Ontario

title: Construction Staging Area - Time Extension - 485 Logan Avenue
topics: construction, construction permits (right-of-way); building, curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way)
brief: DC and F Corporation is building a four-storey residential building at 485 Logan Avenue. Transportation Services asks City Council to continue the construction staging closure of the east sidewalk, a seven-metre-wide portion of the northbound curb lane and the adjacent lane on Logan Avenue, previously approved from July 17, 2020 to April 30, 2021. Because the closure includes bike lanes, City Council approval is required.

title: Construction Staging Area Time Extension - 319-323 Jarvis Street
topics: construction; building
brief: CentreCourt is building a 45-storey residential condominium at 319-323 Jarvis Street. Transportation Services asks City Council to continue the closure of the east sidewalk and a 4.3-metre-wide portion of the northbound curb lane on Jarvis Street for construction staging, previously approved in June 2019. Because the TTC operates on Jarvis Street, City Council approval is required.
address: 319 Jarvis Toronto Ontario; 323 Jarvis Toronto Ontario

title: Construction Staging Area - 2161 Yonge Street (Yonge Street and Soudan Avenue)
topics: construction, construction permits (right-of-way); building, curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way)
brief: Tribute Communities is building a 35-storey mixed-use building at 2161 Yonge Street. Transportation Services asks City Council to close the north sidewalk and a four-metre-wide portion of the westbound curb lane on Soudan Avenue, from July 16, 2021 to June 30, 2024, for a construction staging area. Because the TTC operates on Yonge Street, City Council approval is required.

title: 33-49 Avenue Road and 136-148 Yorkville Avenue - Zoning Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve a zoning amendment for 33-49 Avenue Road and 136-148 Yorkville Avenue. The Ontario Land Tribunal had approved a 29-storey mixed-use building with heritage conservation in 2018; a March 2020 application expanded the site and changed the proposal, and Council approved demolishing the designated heritage property at 33 Avenue Road in November 2020 subject to conditions.
address: 33 Avenue Toronto Ontario; 49 Avenue Toronto Ontario; 136 Yorkville Toronto Ontario; 148 Yorkville Toronto Ontario

title: City- initiated Bloor Street: St. Helen's Avenue to Perth Avenue Planning Framework
topics: urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: City Planning recommends City Council endorse the city-initiated planning framework for Bloor Street from St. Helen's Avenue to Perth Avenue, to guide a future Official Plan amendment and evaluate development applications. The framework sets a vision for a diverse, complete and connected community with heritage properties integrated, a coordinated public realm network, and defined urban structure and built form.
address: Toronto Ontario Bloor St. Helens; Toronto Ontario Bloor Perth

title: King-Spadina Public Realm Strategy
topics: urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: City Planning recommends City Council adopt the King-Spadina Public Realm Strategy. As resident and worker populations grow, the strategy sets a vision and framework to revitalize existing parks and open spaces, create new ones, and connect them through enhanced streetscapes in the historic built-up area.

title: Liberty Village Public Realm and Community Services and Facilities Study - Update
topics: public realm; public spaces
brief: This is an information item: a status update on the Liberty Village Public Realm and Community Services and Facilities Study, covering the terms of reference, community engagement strategy and estimated timelines. City Council is asked to receive it for information.

title: Application to Remove a City-Owned Tree - 1380 Queen Street West
topics: city-owned trees, tree removal; city owned trees; public owned trees; publicly owned trees; trees on public property
brief: The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends City Council deny a permit to remove a City-owned ginkgo tree at 1380 Queen Street West. The 12-centimetre tree is healthy and maintainable, despite concerns its roots could damage water and sprinkler service lines.

title: Intention to Designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - 1354, 1358, and 1360 Queen Street West
topics: heritage designation;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate 1354, 1358, and 1360 Queen Street West under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for their cultural heritage value. The properties were listed on the Heritage Register on December 16, 2020 and sit in the Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District study area.
address: 1354 Queen Toronto Ontario; 1358 Queen Toronto Ontario; 1360 Queen Toronto Ontario

title: Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property - 160 Gerrard Street East (Allan Gardens)
topics: heritage designation;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve alterations to Allan Gardens at 160 Gerrard Street East, a Part IV designated heritage property. The work includes reinstating the central entrance to the Palm House, altering the north and south pavilion entrances and interior doorways, and replacing wall and window glazing with a new aluminum or fibreglass system.

title: Intention to Designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - 600 King Street West
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate 600 King Street West under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property, at the northeast corner of King Street West and Portland Street, holds a four-and-a-half-storey brick building constructed in 1901 to designs by Chadwick and Beckett for the Beatty Manufacturing Company Ltd.

title: 1358-1360 and 1354-1356 Queen Street West and 8-10, 12 and 14 Brock Avenue Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Request for Direction
topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Planning recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal hearing to oppose the Official Plan and zoning amendment applications for 1354-1360 and 1358 Queen Street West and 8-14 Brock Avenue. The applications propose a nine-storey mixed-use building with 117 homes and ground-floor commercial space.
address: 8 Brock Toronto Ontario; 10 Brock Toronto Ontario; 12 Brock Toronto Ontario; 14 Brock Toronto Ontario; 1354 Queen Toronto Ontario; 1356 Queen Toronto Ontario; 1358 Queen Toronto Ontario; 1360 Queen Toronto Ontario

title: 133-141 Queen Street East and 128 Richmond Street East- Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Direction
topics: appeals, rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Planning recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal in opposition to the zoning amendment appeal for 133-141 Queen Street East and 128 Richmond Street East. The October 2019 application proposes a 39-storey mixed-use building; staff say it conflicts with provincial policy and the Official Plan.
address: 131 Queen Toronto Ontario; 141 Queen Toronto Ontario; 128 Richmond Toronto Ontario

title: 386-394 Symington Avenue, 405 Perth Avenue and 17 Kingsley Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Direction
topics: Official Plans, zoning;
brief: City Planning recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal in support of the revised Official Plan and zoning amendment applications for 386-394 Symington Avenue, 405 Perth Avenue and 17 Kingsley Avenue. The proposal is a residential development with a 17-storey tower, an eight-storey portion and a four-storey portion, at a maximum height of 60.3 metres.
address: 17 Kingsley Toronto Ontario; 405 Perth Toronto Ontario; 386 Symington Toronto Ontario; 394 Symington Toronto Ontario

title: 48-110 Eastdale Avenue - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Final Report
topics: development, multi-residential properties, part lot control; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: City Planning recommends City Council enact a part lot control exemption by-law for 48-110 Eastdale Avenue, to create three separate legal parcels for the development of new 35-storey and 7-storey residential buildings plus a 612-square-metre public space, while keeping the existing 24-storey apartment building. The parcels would share a driveway, amenities and underground parking.
address: 48 Eastdale Toronto Ontario; 110 Eastdale Toronto Ontario

title: 101, 111 and 129 St Clair Avenue West - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Final Report
topics: rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Planning recommends City Council enact a part lot control exemption by-law for 101, 111 and 129 St. Clair Avenue West, to align property boundaries with already-poured foundations, establish easements and rights-of-way, and allow potential strata conveyance of the retail space in the restored Deer Park Church at 129 St. Clair Avenue West.
address: 101 St Clair Toronto Ontario; 111 St Clair Toronto Ontario; 129 St Clair Toronto Ontario

title: 571 Dundas Street West - Alexandra Park Revitalization - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Final Report
topics: part lot control, redevelopment; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: City Planning recommends City Council enact a part lot control exemption by-law for 571 Dundas Street West, to create three conveyable lots for Phase 2A of the Alexandra Park Revitalization — including a 13-storey market condominium. A draft plan of subdivision for Phase 2 is under review, with registration anticipated in August 2021.

title: 685 Queen Street East - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Final Report
topics: co-operative housing, demolitions, rental housing; co-op housing; coop housing; cooperative housing, rental properties; rental units
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve Riverdale Co-operative Houses' application to demolish the rear half of the building at 685 Queen Street East, removing nine non-profit co-operative rental homes, and build a five-storey rear addition with 26 new affordable rental homes — a net gain of 17. The facade and front portion would be retained.

title: Permanent Closure of the Public Lane at the Rear of 2104-2110 Yonge Street
topics: lanes, lanes; traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes, traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council permanently close portions of the public lane at the rear of 2104-2110 Yonge Street. Once closed, part of the lane would be sold to the adjacent property owner and part retained by the City, with operational management transferred to the TTC.
address: 2104 Yonge Toronto Ontario; 2110 Yonge Toronto Ontario

title: Inclusion on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register - 19 Parkcrest Drive
topics: heritage designation;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council include 19 Parkcrest Drive on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value. The property holds a one-and-a-half-storey Craftsman bungalow built around 1916-1917 by Frederick J. Cornell, distinguished by rustic cladding of pebbles collected from the Scarborough Bluffs shoreline.

title: Request for Directions Report - 1966 to 2050 Eglinton Avenue East and 50 Thermos Road - Official Plan Amendment Application
topics: official plan amendments;
brief: City Planning recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing to oppose the applicant's appeal of the Official Plan amendment application for 1966 to 2050 Eglinton Avenue East and 50 Thermos Road. The application would add a site-specific policy for a mixed-use development with new public streets and parkland in the Golden Mile Secondary Plan area, demolishing 31,451 square metres of low-rise retail.
address: 1966-2050 Eglinton Toronto Ontario; 50 Thermos Toronto Ontario

title: All-Way Stop Control - Brimley Road South and Barkdene Hills
topics: stop signs; all-way stop controls; technical warrants
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to install all-way stop control at Brimley Road South and Barkdene Hills, to enhance safety as part of the planned Brimley Road South multi-use trail work tied to the Bluffers Park waterfront access plan. Because the TTC operates bus service on Brimley Road South, City Council approval is required.

title: Metrolinx GO Expansion - Permanent Closure of Steeles Avenue East Diversion Road
topics: road closures; street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to permanently close the Steeles Avenue East diversion road between Redlea Avenue and Silver Star Boulevard. The diversion road is no longer needed for Metrolinx's Steeles Avenue East Grade Separation project under the GO Expansion program. Council is also asked to remove the temporary public highway dedication and rescind the related traffic by-laws.

title: Final Report - 2740 Lawrence Avenue East - Zoning Amendment - Subdivision
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve a rezoning and subdivision at 2740 Lawrence Avenue East for 35 detached homes and 65 street townhouses, with a new 18.5-metre public street in a P-loop, a new public park of about 0.25 hectares, and two public walkways.

title: Final Report - 411 Victoria Park Avenue, 2510 and 2530 Gerrard Street East - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment, Subdivision Applications
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, subdivision (land); re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, subdivision of land
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve revised Official Plan, zoning and subdivision applications for 411 Victoria Park Avenue, 2510 and 2530 Gerrard Street East, updating prior approvals for the Birchcliff Quarry Lands that never proceeded. The new concept has five blocks on two new public streets with four mid-rise buildings of 8 to 12 storeys and four townhouse blocks — 1,052 homes, including 120 affordable homes (11.4 percent).
address: 2510 Gerrard Toronto Ontario; 2530 Gerrard Toronto Ontario; 411 Victoria Park Toronto Ontario

title: Upcoming Review of City Affordable Home Ownership Policy and Programs
topics: affordable housing, ownership housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: The Housing Secretariat outlines current and upcoming work on affordable home ownership, including a planned review of the City's affordable home ownership delivery model and policy framework. The review would also implement the Auditor General's recommendations. Council is asked to authorize the Executive Director to hire a consultant for the review.

title: The Future of Yonge and Eglinton's Canada Square: Supporting Midtown Existing and Future Residents' Quality of Life - Special Study Area Report
topics: community development; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: City Planning brings the Special Study Area Report with guiding principles for the Canada Square redevelopment and the Yonge Street corridor north of Eglinton Avenue, as Council requested April 7, 2021. Council is asked to have the Chief Planner consider the vision and priorities in Attachment 1 when reviewing the zoning application for 2180-2210 Yonge Street, 15 Eglinton Avenue West and 20 and 46 Berwick Avenue.
address: 2180-2210 Yonge Toronto Ontario; 20 Berwick Toronto Ontario; 46 Berwick Toronto Ontario; 15 Eglinton Toronto Ontario

title: Alterations to a Heritage Property Designated under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act - 405 Sherbourne Street
topics: heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve alterations to the Part V designated heritage property at 405 Sherbourne Street to allow a 26-storey mixed-use building under the Housing Now Initiative. The building would replace an existing surface parking lot; there are no heritage buildings on the site, but impacts on the adjacent Cabbagetown Northwest Heritage Conservation District are addressed through the design.

title: Housing Now - 405 Sherbourne Street - Zoning Amendment - Final Report
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve a city-initiated zoning amendment for the City-owned parking lot at 405 Sherbourne Street, a Phase Two Housing Now site. The proposal is a 26-storey mixed-use building with 267 rental homes — 33 to 50 percent affordable — plus at least 168 square metres of community facility space for a not-for-profit.

title: Broadening Access to Our City Planning Processes
topics: planning, public consultation; community consultation; consultation; public hearing
brief: Councillor Mike Layton asks City Council to have the City Clerk and Chief Planner report back to the Planning and Housing Committee on actions to remove systemic barriers to public participation in the development application process. Suggested measures include providing translated notice of planning applications so marginalized and working residents can take part.

title: Toronto Tenant Support Program Implementation
topics: supportive housing, tenants; alternative housing; special needs housing; supported housing, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: The Subcommittee on the Protection of Affordable Rental Housing recommends City Council direct the General Manager of Shelter, Support and Housing Administration to implement the Toronto Tenant Support Program as set out in the May 31, 2021 report. The program aligns existing supports for private-market tenants with current market conditions.

title: Tenant Advisory Committee Updates and 2021-2022 Work Plan
topics: tenants, work plans; renters; tenancy agreements
brief: The Subcommittee on the Protection of Affordable Rental Housing recommends City Council have the Housing Secretariat print 750 hard copies of the Eviction Prevention Tool Kit and distribute ten each to every City Councillor's office and to the offices of all Members of Parliament and Members of Provincial Parliament. The recommendation comes with the Tenant Advisory Committee's 2021-2022 work plan update.

title: 1113-1117 Dundas Street West - New Non-Profit Affordable Housing Opportunity
topics: affordable housing, non-profit organizations; affordable homes; housing projects, non profit; nonprofit; not-for-profit organizations
brief: Councillor Joe Cressey asks City Council to direct staff to prepare the paperwork to change the planned disposal of the City-owned properties at 1113 and 1117 Dundas Street West, just east of Ossington Avenue. CreateTO and the Housing Secretariat found good potential for a non-profit affordable housing project there, possibly 100 percent affordable, pending a partner selection process.

title: Housing Now - Bloor-Kipling (Six Points) Block Context Plan and Blocks 1, 2 and 5 City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Final Report
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve a city-initiated zoning amendment for Blocks 1, 2 and 5 of the Bloor-Kipling (Six Points) lands — seven publicly-owned blocks created by decommissioning the Six Points Interchange, including the future Etobicoke Civic Centre site and a new park. Five blocks were approved for Phase 1 of the Housing Now Initiative in 2019.

title: Toronto Green Standard Review and Update
topics: green standards; green development standards; sustainable development standards; toronto green standards
brief: City Planning recommends City Council adopt Toronto Green Standard Version 4 (2022) for new development applications starting May 1, 2022. The Green Standard, updated about every four years since 2010, drives the City toward zero-emissions buildings by 2030 and 2050 greenhouse gas reduction targets.

title: East Harbour Transit Oriented Communities Proposal
topics: community development, transit networks; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: City Planning reports on the provincial government's new mixed-use development proposal at East Harbour, as Council directed in May 2021. Council is asked to tell the Province and Cadillac Fairview it expects robust, timely community engagement led and paid for by Cadillac Fairview, and to direct staff to engage and report back to the Planning and Housing Committee in November and Council in December 2021.

title: Rapid Housing Initiative - 150 Dunn Avenue (Part of a Larger Parcel of Land Including 74, 82, 130, 160, and 162 Dunn Avenue, 1-17 Close Avenue, and 74 and 78 Springhurst Avenue)
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: City Planning and the Housing Secretariat propose a modular housing development at 150 Dunn Avenue (including 74-162 Dunn Avenue, 1-17 Close Avenue and 74-78 Springhurst Avenue) under the Rapid Housing Initiative, creating about 51 supportive homes for people experiencing homelessness with the University Health Network's Gattuso Centre. Council is asked to endorse in principle using a Minister's Zoning Order for zoning relief, and to have staff report back on community engagement.

title: Creating an Additional 92 Affordable Rental Homes at 1750 Ellesmere Road
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize Open Door Program incentives for 92 more affordable rental homes at 1750 Ellesmere Road, bringing the site to 242 affordable rental units. Council approved incentives for 150 units in 2017; the expanded proposal's zoning relief was approved in October 2020 and upheld on appeal. Council is asked to exempt the additional units from development charges and waive building permit, planning and parkland fees.

title: Creating New Affordable Rental Homes at 3377 Bayview Avenue
topics: affordable housing, rental housing; affordable homes; housing projects, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Open Door Program incentives for up to 752 affordable rental homes in the proposed Tyndale Green development on Tyndale University lands at 3377 Bayview Avenue. The project, a partnership between Tyndale University and Markee Developments, is in initial planning stages. Council is asked to authorize fee waivers and a development charge exemption.

title: Technical Amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013 and Former City of North York Zoning By-law 7625 relating to 32x and 34 Woolton Crescent
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Planning recommends City Council enact technical amendments to fix a zoning map error at 32x and 34 Woolton Crescent, where the zone labels were reversed: the conservation authority-owned 32x should be Open Space Natural and the privately owned house at 34 should be Residential Detached. Council is also asked to let the City Solicitor make technical changes.

title: Midtown Infrastructure Implementation Strategies - Interim Report
topics: infrastructure, strategic plans; strategic planning; strategy
brief: City Planning gives an interim report on the Council-directed infrastructure implementation strategies for the Midtown (Yonge-Eglinton) area, covering parks and public realm, community services and facilities, transportation and municipal servicing. Council is asked to adopt the Eglinton Green Line Landscape and Public Realm Standards and use them in assessing development applications on Eglinton Avenue East.

title: Creating 172 New Affordable Rental Homes at 300-304 The East Mall
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Open Door Program incentives for up to 172 affordable rental homes, including 30 supportive housing units, at 300-304 The East Mall (Valhalla Village). KingSett Capital's affordable housing partnership would build the homes as part of a larger mixed-income, mixed-use development, keeping them affordable for at least 40 years. Council is asked to authorize fee waivers, development charge exemptions and a property tax exemption.

title: Concept 2 Keys Development Application Review Program - Q2 2021 Update
topics: affordable housing, development; affordable homes; housing projects, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: This is an information item: the second-quarter 2021 update on the Concept 2 Keys program, which is transforming how the City delivers development review services to be consistent, transparent, collaborative and accountable. The report covers Phase 1 preliminary results and Phase 2 preparatory work. City Council is asked to receive it for information.

title: Modernizing Chapter 489, Grass and Weeds to Streamline Processes and Support Biodiversity
topics: weeds; grass and weeds; long grass; weeds and tall grass
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend Municipal Code Chapter 489 (Grass and Weeds) to modernize the natural garden exemption process, streamline enforcement, and support pollinators and biodiversity. The changes include defining turfgrass and setting its maximum height. The review follows a 2018 Ombudsman report on long grass and weeds complaints.

title: Short-term Rental Updates and Exploring their Conversion to Longer-term Housing
topics: accommodation providers; accommodation services; bed and breakfasts; hotel rooms; hotels; lodging (short term); motels; resorts; student hostels; tourist accommodation; traveller accommodation
brief: Staff report on short-term rentals and the July 2020 request to explore converting STR units to longer-term affordable rental housing, informed by research from Professor David Wachsmuth and McGill's Urban Politics and Governance group. Council is asked to amend Municipal Code Chapter 547 to tighten rules on advertising and facilitating short-term rentals.

title: Geary Works Planning Study and City-Initiated Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment - Final Report
topics: Official Plans, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Planning and Economic Development and Culture bring the final report on Geary Works, a comprehensive study and community vision for Geary Avenue. Council is asked to adopt an area-specific Official Plan amendment and zoning amendment for lands including 1-345 and 2-360 Geary Avenue, plus a cultural heritage resource assessment and other measures from the study's six recommendations.

title: Request for Direction Report -  Zoning By-law Amendment Application - 2 Valleyanna Drive
topics: redevelopment, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: City Planning recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal to oppose the zoning amendment application at 2 Valleyanna Drive in its current form. The application would add a three-storey, 9.6-metre residential addition with four new three-bedroom units, retaining the heritage building as a fifth unit, for 2,096.7 square metres of floor area.

title: Request for Direction Report - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - 50, 60 and 90 Eglinton Avenue West and 17 to 19 Henning Avenue
topics: redevelopment, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: City Planning recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal to oppose the zoning amendment application for 50, 60 and 90 Eglinton Avenue West and 17 and 19 Henning Avenue in its current form. The December 15, 2020 application consolidates the sites under single ownership and revises earlier tower proposals.
address: 17-19 Henning Toronto Ontario; 50-90 Eglinton Toronto Ontario

title: Final Report - Application to Lift Holding Provision (H) - 665, 667, 669 and 671 Sheppard Avenue West
topics: redevelopment, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: City Planning recommends City Council lift the Holding symbol on the zoning for 665, 667, 669 and 671 Sheppard Avenue West, allowing one five-storey and two three-storey buildings. The holding was for sanitary capacity issues; a solution has been found and the works contract awarded, with the Chief Engineer satisfied the work will finish well before occupancy.

title: Consistent Speed Limits on Leslie Street
topics: major arterial roads, safety, speed limits; public safety
brief: Councillor Carroll asks City Council to standardize the speed limit on Leslie Street in Don Valley North to 50 km/h. Residents and parents of Zion Heights Middle School report speeding and near misses where the limit rises from 50 to 60 km/h north of Cummer/McNicoll Avenue. Council is asked to rescind the 60 km/h limit between McNicoll Avenue and Steeles Avenue East and set 50 km/h.

title: Application to Remove a Private Tree - 6 Caines Avenue
topics: privately-owned trees, tree removal; private owned trees; private trees; privately owned trees; trees on private property
brief: The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends City Council deny a permit to remove a privately owned black walnut tree at 6 Caines Avenue. The 49-centimetre tree is healthy and maintainable; the applicant cited falling nuts, toxicity to a pet, and a planned swimming pool.

title: Application to Remove Two Private Trees - 3 Jainey Place
topics: privately-owned trees, tree removal; private owned trees; private trees; privately owned trees; trees on private property
brief: The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends City Council deny a permit to remove two privately owned trees at 3 Jainey Place — a 66-centimetre Norway maple and a 72-centimetre honey locust. The removal was requested for backyard re-landscaping and a rear basement walkout tied to a lot severance; both trees are healthy and maintainable.

title: Application to Remove a Private Tree - 522 Fairlawn Avenue
topics: fences; division fences; line fences
brief: The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends City Council deny a permit to remove a privately owned honey locust at 522 Fairlawn Avenue. The 35-centimetre tree is healthy and maintainable; the removal was requested for a swimming pool and surrounding hardscape.

title: Application to Remove a Private Tree - 294 Fairlawn Avenue
brief: The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends City Council deny a permit to remove a privately owned Norway spruce at 294 Fairlawn Avenue. The 76-centimetre tree is healthy and maintainable, despite the owner's claims that its sap and roots damaged their home, yard and adjacent homes.

title: Final Report - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - 2550 Victoria Park Avenue and 2, 4, 6 Lansing Square
topics: redevelopment, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve a zoning amendment for a master-planned community at 2550 Victoria Park Avenue and 2, 4, 6 Lansing Square: an 18-storey office building and six residential buildings from 4 to 40 storeys, with 3,336.7 square metres of retail, a 4,843-square-metre public park, three new public streets and two public open spaces.
address: 2-6 Lansing Toronto Ontario; 2550 Victoria Park Toronto Ontario

title: Inclusion on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register - 55 St Edmunds Drive
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council include 55 St. Edmunds Drive on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value. The property holds a two-and-a-half-storey stucco house with stone detail built in 1926 to plans by architect William Breden Galbraith, an example of the Tudor Revival style in the Lawrence Park neighbourhood.

title: Intention to Designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - 2 Valleyanna Drive
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate 2 Valleyanna Drive under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property, at the northeast corner of Bayview Avenue and Valleyanna Drive, is a two-storey L-shaped building originally the gatehouse to Dr. Herbert Alexander Bruce's Annandale estate. It has been listed on the Heritage Register since September 27, 2006.

title: Final Report - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - 699 Sheppard Avenue East
topics: official plan amendments, redevelopment, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve an Official Plan and zoning amendment for a 12-storey mixed-use building with 169 homes at 699 Sheppard Avenue East. The building would have 10,829 square metres of floor area including 50.5 square metres of ground-floor commercial space, 115 underground parking spaces and 238 bicycle spaces.

title: Supporting Small Businesses During the Pandemic by Eliminating Unfair Interest Payments - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: disease outbreaks, small businesses; epidemics; pandemics
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Brad Bradford ask City Council to direct the City Manager to review the COVID-19 property tax deferral program and report back to the September 30, 2021 Council meeting on retroactively eliminating interest payments on late payments. The motion notes small businesses were financially devastated by lockdowns through no fault of their own.

title: Support for The Wildseed Centre for Arts and Activism - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: arts and culture;
brief: Councillors Mike Layton and Paula Fletcher ask City Council to increase the 2021 operating budget by $250,000 gross, $0 net, on a one-time basis, for capital upgrades to Black Lives Matter Canada's facility at 24 Cecil Street. The three-storey building, purchased by Black Lives Matter Canada, will become the permanent home of the Wildseed Centre for Arts and Activism, with offices, meeting space, studios and community gathering space.

title: Request to Amend the 2021 Parks, Forestry and Recreation Capital Budget for a Commemorative Plaque in MacGregor Playground - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: parks, plaques; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: Councillors Ana Bailão and Joe Cressy ask City Council to create a new capital sub-project for a commemorative plaque in MacGregor Playground. The plaque would recognize the historic St. Clarens rope walk, an approximately 550-metre lane between Lansdowne Avenue and St. Clarens Avenue used for rope-making for more than 60 years and appearing on maps as early as 1868.

title: Pilot Project to Remove Cow Parsnip from Guild Inn Park Gardens Pathways - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: botanical gardens; botanical plant collection; botanical resources; formal gardens
brief: Councillors Paul Ainslie and Jennifer McKelvie ask City Council to have the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation run a pilot project removing invasive cow parsnip within three metres of all public pathways in the Guild Inn Park and Gardens. The plant is listed by the City as an invasive species dangerous to human health and pets, with sap that can cause blistering and burns when exposed to sunlight.

title: Linear Closure Material and Vino Rosso - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: restaurants; cafeterias; dining; eating places; food premises
brief: Councillors Paula Fletcher and Brad Bradford ask City Council to have Transportation Services work with the operator of Mattachioni restaurant at 1499-1501 Gerrard Street East on its proposed 1.2-metre curbside fence for the CaféTO program. The fence, previously used for another purpose, is 20 centimetres higher than the guidelines allow, but may be safe in that location; the motion is urgent because much of the outdoor dining season will be over by the next Council meeting.

title: 592 Gerrard Street East - Zoning Amendment - Final Report and Licence Arrangement- by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
brief: Councillors Paula Fletcher and Brad Bradford ask City Council to enact a temporary use zoning by-law allowing an outdoor patio in the vacant Toronto Parking Authority surface lot at 592 Gerrard Street East, and to approve a licensing arrangement with nearby restaurants. The bike share station on the lot's frontage would remain.

title: Equitable CafeTO Operating Hours in Willowdale -  by Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Councillors John Filion and Mike Colle ask City Council to exempt certain Willowdale restaurant locations from the CaféTO rule requiring flankage cafés to close by 11:00 p.m., with last alcohol call at 10:15 p.m., while curb-lane and sidewalk-frontage cafés can serve alcohol until 2:00 a.m. The motion says the discrepancy is inequitable for very similar businesses, with Willowdale flankage cafés no closer to residences than those allowed later hours.

title: Authority to Accept Land at 5200 Yonge Street for Use as the Site of a Food Incubator Program - by Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: food, land; menus, property
brief: Councillors John Filion and Mike Colle ask City Council to accept the stratified parcel of land at 5200 Yonge Street that the developer must convey to the City under the Section 37 agreement, for use as the Food Incubator Tenancy Program site. Council approved the program in June 2021 to help small food service businesses start and grow, with below-market leases for four tenants plus a food learning operator.

title: Liquor Licence Application - Orote, 276 Havelock Street - File Number 1151823 - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillors Ana Bailão and Joe Cressy ask City Council to direct the City Clerk to tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor licence for Orote at 276 Havelock Street is not in the public interest. The application is opposed as lacking community support.

title: Approval of a Minor, Minor Variance to the Zoning By-Law for 2 Bloor Street West - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
brief: Councillors Mike Layton and Joe Cressy ask City Council to declare, under subsection 45(1.4) of the Planning Act, that a minor variance application is permitted for 2 Bloor Street West and 820 Yonge Street. The 2020 zoning amendments allow three towers on two parcels divided by a new public park; the applicant seeks changes to the phasing of loading spaces and the location of required office uses in Buildings A and B. The motion is urgent because construction is set to begin.

title: Protecting Jobs in Scarborough - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: employment opportunities, public transit; careers; employment; job applications; job boards; job openings; job opportunities; job postings; job vacancies; jobs; vacancies (jobs), local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Councillors Michael Thompson and Jennifer McKelvie ask City Council to have the Transit Expansion Office and Transportation Services ask Metrolinx to immediately revisit the design of the Progress Avenue grade separation and others on the Stouffville Rail Corridor. The motion says the road-over-rail design under the GO Expansion Program threatens to cut off jobs in Scarborough.

title: Authorization for Submission of Minor Variance Application - 1478-1496 Kingston Road - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: Councillors Gary Crawford and Jennifer McKelvie ask City Council to authorize, under subsection 45(1.4) of the Planning Act, the submission of a minor variance application for 1478-1496 Kingston Road covering setbacks and parking requirements. Site-specific zoning by-laws for the property were enacted in October 2019, and privately initiated amendments normally block variance applications for two years.

title: 401 Logan Avenue - Zoning Amendment - Final Report - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: boulevard cafes, programs, theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities, boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants)
brief: Councillors Paula Fletcher and Ana Bailão ask City Council to enact a temporary use zoning by-law for an outdoor patio with a live performance stage on the surface parking lot at 401 Logan Avenue, associated with the Crow's Theatre Bar and Lounge at 345 Carlaw Avenue. Crow's Theatre has been closed during the pandemic due to limits on indoor public gatherings.

title: 25 The West Mall - Sherway Gardens Temporary Outdoor Patio and Technical Amendment to By-law 198-2021   - Final Report - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Stephen Holyday
topics: boulevard cafes, by-laws; boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants), bylaws
brief: Councillors Mark Grimes and Stephen Holyday ask City Council to enact a zoning by-law amendment for a temporary outdoor patio for restaurants at Sherway Gardens, 25 The West Mall, plus a technical amendment to By-law 198-2021. The patio would sit on private property in the mall's existing parking lot; the mall's food court and restaurants were heavily affected by COVID-19 limits on indoor gatherings.

title: Urgent Authorization Needed to Release Section 37 Funds for Community Safety and Public Realm Improvements to Trolley Crescent - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: community safety, developers, funding, improvement, parking pads, parks, public realm, transportation, waterfronts; boulevard parking; front yard parking; off street parking; off street permit parking, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, enhancement; rehabilitation (property), financing, lakefronts; waterfront trail, public spaces, transportation services
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Joe Cressy ask City Council to release $260,808 in Section 37 funds from the 46 to 48 Power Street and 113 to 125 Parliament Street development for community safety and public realm improvements at Trolley Crescent. Since 2015, vehicles have illegally entered and driven through Underpass Park, and a pedestrian was struck in summer 2020; staff are studying long-term fixes including fencing and vehicle gates.

title: 390 and 440 Dufferin Street - Small Business Incubation Centre - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: leasing, mixed use areas, municipal officials, property owners, redevelopment, small businesses, urban planning, zoning bylaws; building owners; land owners; property ownership, city officials, city planning; community planning; regional planning, leases, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Councillors Ana Bailão and Brad Bradford ask City Council to direct the Chief Planner to enter an amending agreement to the 2016 Section 37 agreement for 390 and 440 Dufferin Street and 41 Alma Avenue, to implement the Small Business Incubation Centre. The 2016 settlement requires the redevelopment's three 9-to-13-storey mixed-use buildings to provide two floors to the City for 25 years at subsidized rents for the centre; the City selected a sub-lessee and operator in June 2019.

title: Musician Rehearsal Spaces in the City of Toronto - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: arts and culture, buskers, costs, economic development, music, performers; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, entertainers, sidewalk artists; street performers; street entertainers; street musicians
brief: Councillors Ana Bailão and Brad Bradford ask City Council to have the City Manager, the Chief Planner and Economic Development and Culture review the inventory, availability, cost and status of musician rehearsal space in Toronto. Live music was among the hardest-hit sectors in the pandemic, and rehearsal space, especially in areas like the Geary neighbourhood, is under threat and diminishing.

title: Modular Housing Initiative - Phase Two - 7 Glamorgan Avenue - Final Report - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: housing, planning; homes; residences
brief: Councillors Ana Bailão and Michael Thompson ask City Council to adopt the Chief Planner and Housing Secretariat's final proposal for modular housing at 7 Glamorgan Avenue, and to request the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing make a Minister's Zoning Order to provide the needed zoning relief. Council endorsed the Phase Two proposal in principle at its June 8 and 9, 2021 meeting.

title: 1637-1645 Bathurst Street - Amendment to Zoning By-law - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: planning, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Councillors Josh Matlow and Mike Layton ask City Council to amend the draft zoning by-law amendments for 1637-1645 Bathurst Street to allow a minimum accessible parking space width of 3.4 metres. Council approved the 4-storey, 75-unit apartment building (including 27 rental replacement units) with 93 underground parking spaces in December 2020; site plan review found the accessible parking width needs the change.

title: Completing The Missing Link and Building the East Toronto Railpath - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: bridge construction; bridge reconstruction
brief: Councillors Mike Layton and Joe Cressy ask City Council to have the City Manager evaluate buying the rail path lands and the Half-Mile Bridge from Metrolinx, plus an adjacent property above Nesbitt Drive, to create the East Toronto Railpath, and report back to Council as needed. The 350-metre former Canadian Pacific Railway viaduct over the Don River could link Don Valley public spaces and relieve crowded trails.

title: Request to Amend the 2021 Parks, Forestry and Recreation Capital Budget for Charlton Park and Harlandale Park Playground Improvements - by Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: budgets, parks; budgets and accounts, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillors John Filion and Shelley Carroll ask City Council to amend the Parks, Forestry and Recreation capital budget and plan to add $0.160 million for playground improvements at Charlton Park and Harlandale Park through the Play Enhancement Program. The program's total cost would rise from $11.607 million to $11.767 million; public consultation showed a need for equipment engaging a broader range of ages.

title: Supporting Black-Owned and Operated Businesses in Little Jamaica- by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: neighbourhoods, small businesses; cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods
brief: Councillors Josh Matlow and Mike Layton ask City Council to have Economic Development and Culture, with the Chief Planner and City Planning, report on the feasibility of barring chain stores, known as formula retail, to protect Black-owned and operated businesses in Little Jamaica. The motion says rising rents, Crosstown LRT construction and the COVID-19 pandemic have shuttered many historic businesses in the Caribbean community hub.

title: Ensuring Accountability and Reflecting the Community's Expectations in Preserving and Protecting the Future of Little Jamaica - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: business improvement areas, neighbourhoods; business improvement associations; BIA, cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods
brief: Councillors Josh Matlow and Mike Layton ask City Council to have the Little Jamaica Interdivisional Team consult key stakeholders — including BlackUrbansimTO, the Mayor's Roundtable on Black Business, Reclaim, Rebuild, Eglinton Avenue West, CP Planning and the Black Business and Professional Association — on preserving and protecting the future of Little Jamaica. The motion follows Council's 2020 unanimous adoption of a sustainability plan for Black-owned businesses and a heritage preservation motion for the area.

title: Authority to Enter into a Funding Agreement with PortsToronto and Fund Design and Construction for Rehabilitation of the Ship Channel Bridge Approach Spans and Bascule Bridge - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: bridge rehabilitation, construction, funding, ports, transportation; bridge reconstruction; bridge repair, building, financing, transportation services
brief: Councillors Jennifer McKelvie and Paula Fletcher ask City Council to authorize Transportation Services to negotiate a funding agreement with PortsToronto for rehabilitating the Cherry Street Ship Channel bridge approach spans and the Bascule bridge. The City would contribute up to $22 million from its 2021-2030 capital budget for design and construction over 2021-2025, while PortsToronto rehabilitates the bridge's lifting mechanisms at a cost of about $12 million.

title: Release of Section 37 Funds to The Garden Club of Toronto for Capital Improvements to the Meadoway Project - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: improvement, planning; enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: Councillors Michael Thompson and Gary Crawford ask City Council to release $100,000 in Section 37 funds to the Garden Club of Toronto for capital improvements to the Meadoway project. The registered charity is designing and planting a new park on the Meadoway on the west side of Pharmacy Avenue, just north of Rannock Street, as a community gathering place.

title: Implementing the TOcore Parks and Public Realm Plan in South West Downtown - by Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
brief: Councillors Joe Cressy and Mike Layton ask City Council to have the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation, with the Chief Planner and City Planning, advance coordinated planning and implementation of the Downtown Parks and Public Realm Plan for the south and west downtown neighbourhoods. Rapid growth has strained existing parks, and the motion calls for advancing initiatives including the Core Circle and the Shoreline Stitch.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 funds from the Development at 39 Park Lawn Road to Complete the Berry Road Food Co-op - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: stores; retail stores; shops
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, asks City Council to increase the 2021 operating budget by $50,000 gross, $0 net, fully funded by Section 37 funds from the Park Lawn Road development, to complete the Berry Road Food Co-op project. The not-for-profit food co-op addresses a food desert in the Stonegate neighbourhood; its March 2020 opening was delayed by the pandemic, straining its resources.

title: Agreement with 65 King East GP Inc. or 65 King East LP (Carttera Developments) - streetscape improvements on Colborne Street, Colborne Lane and Leader Lane as part of development of 65 King Street East - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: development; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to authorize Transportation Services to negotiate and enter agreements with 65 King East GP or LP (Carttera Developments) to design and build streetscape improvements on Colborne Street between Church Street and Leader Lane, and on Leader Lane between King Street East and Colborne Street. The developer now wants to expand the scope to include Colborne Lane.

title: Ensuring Retention of Community Benefits Through Provincial Expropriation of Municipally-owned Land - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: community benefits, expropriations; compulsory purchase; eminent domain
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Joe Cressy ask City Council to direct the Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management to report to the September 23, 2021 Executive Committee meeting with recommendations letting Councillors bring business transactions related to provincial expropriation of City-owned land for transit back to Council for approval. The motion concerns the Province's expropriation of municipal land for transit projects under the Expropriations Act and the Building Transit Faster Act.

title: Checking the Ticket - Understanding The Province’s Extraordinary Powers to Expropriate for Transit - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Joe Cressy ask City Council to direct the City Manager to report to the September 23, 2021 Executive Committee meeting on the Province's use of extraordinary expropriation powers for transit projects like the Ontario Line, Scarborough Subway Extension, Yonge North Subway Extension and Eglinton Crosstown West Extension. Questions include how many meetings City staff have had with Metrolinx and whether the Province must properly compensate the City, for example for 271 Front Street East.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto District School Board for Ossington-Old Orchard Junior Public School Playground - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: playground equipment; park equipment; play apparatus; play equipment; play structures
brief: Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to release $205,000 in Section 37 funds from the 871 to 899 College Street development to the Toronto District School Board for Ossington-Old Orchard Junior Public School. The money would fund accessibility improvements, a natural play area, a walkway loop and better basketball courts.

title: Endorsing the call for a Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: climate change; climate protection
brief: Councillors Mike Layton and Shelley Carroll ask City Council to formally endorse the call for a Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty and to have the City Manager write to the Prime Minister asking the federal government to negotiate one. The motion cites the 2018 IPCC warning that net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by mid-century are needed to limit warming to 1.5 degrees, and notes Toronto's hotter summers, intense rainfall and severe winter storms.

title: Grass Cutting Services - Operations Completed by Transportation Services - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Michael Ford
topics: turf maintenance; grass cutting; grass repairs
brief: Councillors Stephen Holyday and Michael Ford ask City Council to have the General Manager of Transportation Services review the service level for the right-of-way grass cutting contracts, including the number of cuts per year on boulevards, traffic islands and centre medians. Budget-driven service reductions have drawn complaints about overgrown and poorly maintained vegetation in Etobicoke Centre.

title: Reviewing suggested solutions to reduce the impact of flooding in the Rockcliffe-Smythe area - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: flooding; floods
brief: Councillors Frances Nunziata and Ana Bailão ask City Council to have Transportation Services and Toronto Water work with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority on naturalizing the Black Creek Channel as part of flood mitigation for the Rockcliffe-Smythe area. Properties in the regulatory floodplain suffer surface and basement flooding during severe storms.

title: Request to amend the 2021 Parks, Forestry and Recreation Capital Budget for Cy Townsend Park Improvements - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Layton
topics: park maintenance, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, parks maintenance
brief: Councillors Josh Matlow and Mike Layton ask City Council to amend the Parks, Forestry and Recreation capital budget and plan to create a $0.042 million sub-project for a new shade structure and safety fence around the perimeter of Cy Townsend Park, which abuts a busy road. The work is fully funded by Section 45 funds from the development at 109 Vaughan Road.

title: 100 Indian Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Final Report - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: boulevard cafes, sports clubs; badminton clubs; baseball associations; baseball leagues; bowling clubs; cross-country ski clubs; curling clubs; gymnastic clubs; hockey associations; hockey leagues; karate clubs; lacrosse clubs; lawn bowling clubs; ride clubs; rifle clubs; slo-pitch leagues; soccer clubs; soccer leagues; softball associations; softball leagues; swim clubs; tennis clubs; volleyball clubs, boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants)
brief: Councillors Gord Perks and Mike Layton ask City Council to enact a zoning by-law amendment letting the High Park Club at 100 Indian Road temporarily expand its outdoor patio into part of the north parking lot and the rear second-storey balcony. Both areas are private property and not part of the CaféTO program; the club wants to expand its existing licensed patio.

title: Determining the feasibility of restricting the retail sale of consumer fireworks - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Mark Grimes
topics: fireworks; firecrackers
brief: Councillors Frances Nunziata and Mark Grimes ask City Council to have Municipal Licensing and Standards and the Fire Chief report in the fourth quarter of 2021 to the General Government and Licensing Committee on the feasibility of restricting the retail sale of consumer fireworks. The motion cites property damage, harm to children and youth, distress to animals, and pollution from firework displays.

title: Advancing Reconciliation and Justice - Assistance to Thunder Woman Healing Lodge - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: First Nations; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Mayor John Tory, asks City Council to authorize acquiring lands at fair market value from the Thunder Woman Healing Lodge Society and providing financial relief from taxes, fees and charges toward developing and operating the future Thunder Woman Healing Lodge at 2217 Kingston Road. The motion calls this a tangible step toward reconciliation and justice; construction was anticipated to begin September 22, 2021.

title: Mitigating community concerns: Refining the Metrolinx Durham-Scarborough Bus Rapid Transit Proposal  - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: bus routes, regional transportation agencies; commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies
brief: Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Mayor John Tory, asks City Council to have the Transit Expansion Office and City Planning ask Metrolinx to further engage the Highland Creek community on the Durham-Scarborough Bus Rapid Transit proposal. Residents are concerned about curbed lanes along a 2.4-kilometre stretch of Ellesmere Road between Military Trail and Kingston Road, where homes sit on both sides and the design is seen as a pinch point.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to fund the Creation and Installation of a Heritage Plaque to Honour Toronto Public Health - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: plaques, public health; heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, asks City Council to increase Heritage Toronto's 2021 operating budget by $7,500, $0 net, for a heritage plaque near Bay Street and Queen Street West recognizing the history of Toronto Public Health. The City's first Medical Officer of Health, Dr. William Canniff, was appointed in 1883 when infectious diseases like cholera, diphtheria, typhus and tuberculosis were common.
address: 20-26 Lombard Toronto Ontario; 25 Richmond Toronto Ontario

title: Re-opening of 88 Queen Street East - Development Charges Deferral - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: development charges;
brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Joe Cressy ask City Council to amend its April 7, 2021 decision deferring development charges for 88 Queen Street East, deleting Part 1 and replacing it. The change authorizes the Chief Building Official and Executive Director of Toronto Building, with the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer, to carry out the deferral while the City's development charges by-law review, due in early 2022, is underway.

title: Authorization to convert a cash-in-lieu Section 37 payment to an in-kind contribution for the construction of a PATH tunnel beneath Simcoe Street by Cadillac Fairview (Frontside Developments LP) - by Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: underground walkways; PAT
brief: Councillors Joe Cressy and Mike Layton ask City Council to convert the Section 37 cash contribution from the development at 156-174 Front Street West and 43-51 Simcoe Street into an in-kind contribution for a PATH tunnel connection toward Union Station. Council would increase the 2021 operating budget by $1,776,997.84 gross, $0 net, fully funded by the Section 37 money already received.
address: 156-174 Front Toronto Ontario; 43-51 Simcoe Toronto Ontario

title: Taking Action to Protect Tenants from Extreme Heat - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow

brief: Councillors Kristyn Wong-Tam and Josh Matlow ask City Council to direct the Executive Director of Municipal Licensing and Standards, the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration, the Director of Environment and Energy, the Chief Resilience Officer, and request the Medical Officer of Health, to take action protecting tenants from extreme heat. brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council direct the Transit Expansion Office, Corporate Real Estate Management, City Planning, and CreateTO to report as soon as possible on provincial interest in the historic First Parliament site at Front Street East and Parliament Street. The northwestern portion of the block is owned by the Province through the Ontario Heritage Trust; the rest, at 271 Front Street East and 25 Berkeley Street, is City-owned.
