brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends that City Council release $12,000 in Section 37 funds from various developments to Community Matters Toronto for eight Bell box murals in Ward 8 (Eglinton-Lawrence). The Bell Box Murals Project replaces graffiti with original art by local artists.

title: Protecting and Preserving Independent Live Performance Venues and Drag Bars - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: performing arts, theatrical performances; musicals; plays; theatrical productions
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council ask the City Manager and the Chief Financial Officer to explore expanding the Creative Co-Location Facilities property tax subclass to independent live performance venues such as drag bars and small theatres. These venues, including safe performance spaces for the LGBTQ2S+ community, were already struggling before the pandemic with high rents and development pressure.

title: Securing Funding for Supportive Housing in Toronto - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: supportive housing; alternative housing; special needs housing; supported housing
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends that City Council keep pressing the Province to fund the operation of 1,100 supportive housing units the City is on track to deliver in 2021 with federal support, and ask the City Manager to report on advocacy options. The Province's March 24 budget did not commit the operating funding needed for the units and their on-site support services. The City is on track to deliver 1,250 new supportive housing units in total.

title: I'm Walking Here - Clarifying No Exit Signage for Pedestrians - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: accessibility, council meetings, maps, neighbourhoods, pedestrians, residents, signs; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods, pedestrianization, signage
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, recommends that City Council ask the General Manager of Transportation Services to report to the July 5, 2021 Infrastructure and Environment Committee on clarifying No Exit signage where pedestrian or cyclist access is still possible. A crowd-sourced map found over 350 locations across the city where No Exit signs block through-traffic but pedestrians can get through.

title: Authorization to Amend the Approved 2021 Operating Budget to Reflect Potential Receipt of a Grant from the Ministry of Labour for xoTO Screen Industry Pathways Programming - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: operating budgets;
brief: Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends that City Council increase the 2021 Economic Development and Culture operating budget by $800,000 gross, zero net, conditional on a grant agreement with the Ontario Ministry of Labour, Training and Skills Development. The City's Film, Television and Digital Media Office applied to the province's $115 million Skills Development Fund for xoTO Screen Industry Pathways programming.

title: 14 Penaire Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: municipal officials, zoning; city officials
brief: Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends that City Council authorize the City Solicitor and staff to support the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of the consent and minor variance applications for 14 Penaire Street at the Toronto Local Appeal Body. The applications would sever the property into two undersized lots with a detached dwelling on each; planning staff said they did not meet the intent of the Official Plan or zoning.

title: Call on Toronto City Council to Confront Anti-Asian Racism and to Move Forward with an Action Plan - by Councillor Cynthia Lai, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: racial discrimination; anti-racism; racism
brief: Councillor Cynthia Lai, seconded by Mayor John Tory, recommends that City Council condemn the recent acts of anti-Asian hate and restate its commitment to an inclusive city, and ask the Mayor to continue the Mayor's Roundtable efforts on the issue. Toronto Police reported anti-Asian hate crimes up 51 percent in 2020 over 2019 and up another 47 percent in 2021, and the motion calls for an action plan to confront anti-Asian racism.

title: Section 37 contribution towards the Joshua Glover Memorial at 4208 Dundas Street West - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: funding; financing
brief: Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson, recommends that City Council allocate $75,856.91 in Section 37 funds to a public art memorial for Joshua Glover at 4208 Dundas Street West. Glover escaped slavery in 1852 and made his way to Etobicoke; his story played a key role in the abolition of slavery in the United States.

title: The Future of Yonge and Eglinton's Canada Square: Supporting Midtown Residents' Quality of Life - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam
topics: community benefits, quality of life;
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, recommends that City Council ask the Chief Planner to establish a working group with the Ward Councillor, residents' and tenants' associations, BIAs, and community organizations on the future of the Canada Square lands at Yonge and Eglinton. The former bus barns site has sat derelict for almost two decades and will become one of Toronto's most important transit hubs.

title: Section 37 contribution towards streetscape improvements at St. Clair Avenue East and O'Connor Drive - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: community improvement plans;
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends reallocating $50,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 1401 O'Connor Drive, currently earmarked for the Topham Park Clubhouse Improvements project, to streetscape enhancements at St. Clair Avenue East and O'Connor Drive under an existing road reconstruction project. The O'Connor Drive Avenue Study was adopted by Council in 2012.

title: Request to Demolish Non-Residential Building at 911X Castlefield Avenue - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: demolitions;
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends that City Council further amend its decision on the non-residential building demolition at 911X Castlefield Avenue, deleting the conditions requiring a beautification agreement and replacing them with the owner's accepted letter of commitment to the beautification plan. City Planning staff have no objections. The item requires re-opening.

title: Authorize the Receipt of Funds and Allocation of Section 37 Funds towards the Nathan Phillips Square Indian Residential School Survivors Restoration of Identity Project - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: First Nations; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council authorize receiving up to $4,000,000 from Toronto Council Fire Native Cultural Centre and allocate $2,000,000 in Section 37 funds to the 2021-2030 capital plan for the Nathan Phillips Square Indian Residential School Survivors Restoration of Identity Project. Since 2017 the City has partnered with Council Fire on the project, fulfilling the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's Call to Action 82.

title: Support for the Canadian Union of Postal Worker's Delivering Community Power Program to Support Expanded Services and Climate Action at Canada Post - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: climate change; climate protection
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends that City Council endorse the Canadian Union of Postal Workers' Delivering Community Power program, which proposes using the public postal network to confront climate change, expand services, and bring financial inclusion to unbanked communities, and send the endorsement to the federal Minister of Public Services and Procurement. No other decision is attached.

title: Officially Recognizing Toronto as a Certified Bird Friendly City - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: bird-friendly development guidelines; lights out toronto
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends that City Council support Toronto becoming a certified Bird Friendly City through Nature Canada, and direct the City Manager to explore partnering with Birds Canada on a Toronto Bird Celebration. A Council resolution is one of the program's requirements; Toronto was the first North American city with bird-friendly policies.

title: Authorization to receive donation revenues for the Black Cultural Centre within the Municipally-owned building at 756 Bathurst Street - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: cultural facilities, donation; art centres; arts centres; cultural attractions; cultural centres, bequest; toy drive
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council authorize the Director of Strategic Partnerships to accept donations to retrofit the municipally owned building at 756 Bathurst Street, under the City's donations policy for community benefits. The building will be the permanent home of A Different Booklist Cultural Centre, which supports Toronto's Black and Caribbean communities.

title: What's In A Name? Getting The Names Right In Our Neighbourhood Profiles - by Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam
topics: neighbourhoods; cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods
brief: Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, recommends that City Council direct the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration to report back to the Economic and Community Development Committee on a process to revise the newly adopted names in the City's Neighbourhood Profiles, in consultation with communities. The City expanded its recognized neighbourhoods from 140 to 158 without input from Council or local councillors on the new names.

title: Excessive Salt Use on Our Sidewalks - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: council meetings, maintenance, residents, road salt management, sidewalks, winter;
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, recommends that City Council ask the General Manager of Transportation Services to review and update the Salt Management Plan for sidewalk salt use, including maximum application rates, vehicle calibration, operator training, and spill handling. Residents in the sidewalk snow clearing pilot say winter maintenance vehicles spread excessive salt that is wasteful, harmful to the environment, and hard on animals.

title: Protecting and Creating Affordable Homes in the Kensington Market Neighbourhood - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council provide $3,000,000 to the Kensington Market Community Land Trust to acquire, renovate, and operate 54-56 Kensington Avenue as affordable rental housing with ground-floor retail, keeping its 12 units affordable for 99 years. The building's tenants have already faced the threat of renoviction as affordable rentals are converted or demolished across the city.

After approval, Toronto Hydro identified a conflict between the west side of the 1182 King building and Hydro infrastructure on the east side of the lot, requiring revised zoning.

brief: Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends a technical correction to Council's February 2021 approval for the Victory Silos redevelopment at 315 and 359 Lake Shore Boulevard. title: Representation at a Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing for 91 McCowan Road - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson

brief: Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, recommends that City Council ask the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to consult with City staff, TABIA, and Toronto Hydro on reducing the cost of covering hydro distribution wires for small businesses doing building maintenance. One property was quoted $19,351 and another $43,825 for the same 17-foot distance, making critical repairs prohibitive.

The Committee of Adjustment refused the applications at its November 2020 hearing.

brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council support the request from Save Jimmie Simpson and the Lakeshore East Community Advisory Committee for a federal environmental assessment of the above-ground section of the Ontario Line through Riverside and Leslieville. Council has previously asked Metrolinx for the business case, community impacts, mitigation measures, and cost comparisons for running the line underground.

title: Preserving the Past, and Protecting the Future of Little Jamaica - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson, recommends that City Council direct the Chief Planner to prioritize a survey of Little Jamaica's cultural heritage resources in the 2021 and 2022 City Planning study work program, as part of the Council-adopted Little Jamaica Cultural District study. Eglinton Avenue West holds Toronto's highest concentration of Black and Caribbean-owned businesses, whose character is threatened by rising rents, LRT construction, and the pandemic.

title: Improving Virtual Community Consultation Meetings for Development Applications - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: public consultation, public health emergency; community consultation; consultation; public hearing
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends that City Council direct the Chief Planner to review virtual community consultation meetings for development applications, consulting with members of the public, and report back to the Planning and Housing Committee in the second quarter of 2021 with recommendations. Virtual meetings have continued through the pandemic, but there are opportunities to improve the public's experience.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 4 and 6 Tippett Road to Community Matters Toronto for Painting Mural Art on 13 Bell Utility Boxes in York-Centre - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jaye Robinson

brief: The General Manager of Solid Waste Management Services recommends that City Council direct the division to join the Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks' South London Air Monitoring Network pilot, which will monitor odour and weather patterns at the City's Green Lane Landfill. The network uses technology to visualize odour emissions, identify sources, and predict odour trajectories.

brief: The General Manager of Solid Waste Management Services and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend that the Infrastructure and Environment Committee approve an additional $900,000 (net of taxes) to the blanket contract with Municipal Maintenance Incorporated for mechanical litter removal services, raising the contract value from $8,268,979 to $9,168,979. The increase addresses an underestimate of winter service hours required over the five-year term.

title: Safe Opening of the Barry Zuckerman Amphitheatre
topics: concerts, theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities
brief: Councillor James Pasternak recommends that City Council direct the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation, with the Medical Officer of Health, to report back to the April 28, 2021 Infrastructure and Environment Committee on safely opening and operating the Earl Bales (Barry Zuckerman) Amphitheatre in summer 2021. The 1,500-seat outdoor venue rarely fills past 20 percent capacity and allows for physical distancing.

brief: Councillor James Pasternak recommends that City Council direct the General Manager of Solid Waste, with the Medical Officer of Health, to report back to the April 28, 2021 Infrastructure and Environment Committee with a safety plan for Environment Days, including a possible drive-through format. The events let thousands of residents drop off household items for reuse, recycling, and safe disposal of hazardous materials.

The delegation would help the TTC meet accessibility requirements.

title: Changes to Community Council Delegations, Authorization of Designated Speed Limit Areas - 30 Kilometres Per Hour on Public Lanes and Local Roads, and Designation of Reserved Lane and Speed Limits on Reserved Lane for Eglinton Avenue Light Rail Transit Segregated Right of Way

brief: The General Manager of Transportation Services recommends that City Council establish designated speed limit areas with 30 km/h limits on public lanes, alleys, and local roads under the Vision Zero Speed Management Strategy, and delegate establishing those designations to community councils. Council is asked to authorize the bike lane installations and by-law amendments. More 2021 projects will come in later reports.

brief: The General Manager of Transportation Services recommends that City Council ask Transportation Services to keep pursuing opportunities for more space for pedestrians, cyclists, and public transit where possible, under public health advice and the City's recovery planning. brief: The Deputy City Manager for Infrastructure and Development Services recommends that City Council authorize working with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority and Waterfront Toronto to finalize the environmental study report and issue a notice of completion for the Broadview and Eastern Flood Protection environmental assessment. The preferred alternative is a flood protection landform along the east side of the Don Valley Parkway and Don River, built in phases.

brief: This is an information item: Councillor Shelley Carroll has submitted an administrative inquiry under Municipal Code S27-61 seeking an update on collective bargaining and labour relations underway at the City and its agencies, boards, and commissions, including the status of negotiations and arbitrations and how Council is kept informed of mandate-setting. Council and the Board are asked to request that the Province collect socio-demographic and ethnic data on vaccinations and give Toronto Public Health access to it.

brief: The Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management recommends that City Council amend the lease with the Shining Through Centre for Children with Autism for 305 Greenfield Avenue to add a five-year renewal option, a termination right, and a six-month fixturing period. The council, a Board of Health advisory body, has faced years of diminished funding and a difficult pandemic year.

title: Reaffirming Support for our Medical Officer of Health and a Public Health-Informed Approach
topics: boards of health;
brief: Councillor Joe Cressy recommends that the Board of Health reaffirm its support for Medical Officer of Health Dr. Eileen de Villa and the entire Toronto Public Health team, and continue to support a public health-informed approach. The motion recognizes their tireless pandemic work and the difficult, at times unpopular, recommendations they have had to make.

title: City Council Approved Toronto Public Health 2021 Operating Budget
topics: boards of health, operating budgets;
brief: This is an information item: the Board of Health receives an update on the Toronto Public Health 2021 Operating Budget approved by City Council on February 18, 2021. Council approved $344,744.2 thousand gross and $124,391.4 thousand net, up $64,073.3 thousand gross (22.8 percent) from the prior year. The Medical Officer of Health recommends the board receive the report for information. No decision is attached.

title: City Council Approved Toronto Public Health 2021-2030 Capital Budget and Plan
topics: boards of health, capital budgets;
brief: This is an information item: the Board of Health receives an update on the Toronto Public Health 2021 Capital Budget and 2022-2030 Capital Plan as approved by City Council on February 18, 2021. The Medical Officer of Health recommends the board receive the report for information. No decision is attached.

title: Ontario Public Health Standards Risk Management Reporting
topics: public health, standards;
brief: This is an information item: the Board of Health receives an update on the risk management reporting required under the Ontario Public Health Accountability Framework, under which public health units report an annual Risk Management Plan to the Ministry of Health. The Medical Officer of Health recommends the board receive the report for information. No decision is attached.

title: Student Nutrition Program: Provincial Funding During COVID-19
topics: disease outbreaks, funding, nutrition, students; diet; dieting; healthy eating, epidemics; pandemics, financing
brief: This is an information item: the Board of Health receives a report on the status of additional emergency provincial funding for student nutrition programs during the pandemic, responding to a January 2021 board motion. Toronto Public Health continues to monitor the situation with schools and works with student nutrition programs, school boards, and their foundations. The Medical Officer of Health recommends the board receive the report for information. No decision is attached.

title: Toronto Urban Health Fund Program - Administration Changes
topics: appointments, boards of health, change; amendments; conversion; modification
brief: The Medical Officer of Health recommends that the Board of Health approve changes to how the Toronto Urban Health Fund program is administered, including revised terms of reference for the review panel and the Indigenous review panel. The fund's administration is supported by two Board of Health committees, and the City recently moved to an online grant management system.

brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel approve awarding a contract to Altec Industries Ltd. for the supply and delivery of three heavy trucks with aerial towers and chipper bodies for the Fleet Services Division, with an option to buy four more. Altec's evaluated bid price was $1,179,174 and it was the only bidder.

title: Award of Ariba Doc Number 2755600779 to VHA Home HealthCare for the Provision of Enterstomal Therapy and Intravenous Therapy for Seniors Services and Long-Term Care

brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel approve awarding a contract to VHA Home HealthCare for enterstomal therapy and intravenous therapy for the City's Seniors Services and Long-Term Care Division. VHA's bid of $202,213.50 was the only bid received.

title: Award of Ariba Doc Number 2706059734 to WSP Canada Inc. for Replacement of Sanitary Forcemains in Various Toronto Locations Group 2 for the Engineering and Construction Services Division

brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel approve awarding a contract to WSP Canada Inc. for professional engineering services for the design and construction of sanitary forcemain replacements at various Toronto locations (Group 2), for Engineering and Construction Services. Three proposals were received.

title: Award of Ariba Doc Number 2682556437 to Exergy Associates Ltd. for the Non-Exclusive Supply, Delivery, of Water Audit and Verification Services Relating to the Capacity Buy Back and Industrial Water Rate Programs for The City of Toronto's Water Division
topics: purchasing, water; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders
brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel approve awarding a contract to Exergy Associates Ltd. for non-exclusive water audit and verification services for the Capacity Buy Back and Industrial Water Rate programs, for Toronto Water. Exergy's bid of $234,756 was the lowest of three bids.

title: Award of Ariba Doc Number 2664382641 to J&J Trailers Manufacturers and Sales Inc. for the Supply and Delivery of Twenty-Two (22) Trailers in Various Configurations for Fleet Services Division

brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel approve awarding a contract to J&J Trailers Manufacturers and Sales Inc. for the supply and delivery of 22 trailers in various configurations for the Fleet Services Division, with an option to buy eight more in 2022. J&J's evaluated bid price was $619,597 and it was the only bidder.

brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel approve awarding a contract to M.E. Andrews and Associates Limited for professional services for the Sewer Rehabilitation Program Management for 2022-2024, for Toronto Water. Four proposals were received; one did not meet the minimum technical threshold.

title: Award of Ariba Doc Number 2601063937 to East Court Ford Lincoln Ltd. for the Supply and Delivery of Five (5) Latest Model, Medium Utility Trucks for Fleet Services Division
topics: city vehicles, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet
brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel approve awarding a contract to East Court Ford Lincoln for the supply and delivery of five latest-model medium utility trucks for the Fleet Services Division. East Court's bid of $1,143,244.73 was the lower of two bids for the truck tables it won.

title: Chair's Update on COVID-19 and TO Live

topics: employment termination; employee exit; layoff; termination of employment
brief: This is an information item: the City Clerk's Office advises that Steve Levitan has resigned from the Board of Directors of TO Live, effective February 12, 2021. The Public Appointments Secretariat is leading recruitment to bring a nominated candidate to City Council. No decision is attached.

title: Digital Transformation—Customer Relationship Management
body: Board of Directors of TO Live
topics: customer service;
brief: The President and CEO of TO Live asks the Board of Directors to approve the Customer Relationship Management solution as part of the organization's Digital Transformation project, as set out in Confidential Attachment 1, and to keep the attachment confidential because it contains the organization's plans and procedures. No other decision is attached.

title: 2021 Programming Risk Budget
body: Board of Directors of TO Live
topics: budgets, operating budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: The President and CEO of TO Live asks the Board of Directors to approve the programming risk budget for the 2021 programming year, as set out in Confidential Attachments 1 and 2, and to authorize public release of the program names and project descriptions once they are publicly announced. The attachments remain confidential.

title: Cyber Security Update
body: Board of Directors of TO Live
topics: security, software; computer programs
brief: This is an information item: the TO Live Audit Committee recommends that the Board of Directors receive an update on the organization's cyber security controls and risks. Confidential Attachment 1 is to remain confidential because it concerns the security of the board's property. No decision is attached.

title: 2020 Fourth Quarter Financial Results and Commentary
body: Board of Directors of TO Live
topics: annual reports, financial reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural item: the TO Live Audit Committee presents the 2020 fourth quarter financial results to the Board of Directors for approval. The board is also asked to keep Confidential Attachment 1 confidential because it contains financial information. No other decision is attached.

title: 2021 State of Good Repair and Facility Fee Reserve Fund
body: Board of Directors of TO Live
topics: funding; financing
brief: The TO Live Audit Committee recommends that the Board of Directors approve the 2021 State of Good Repair and Facility Fee Reserve Fund capital projects, including 2021 projects with multi-year components, and related purchase orders and tender awards, as set out in Confidential Attachment 1.

title: TO Live - 2021 Goals and Objectives
body: Board of Directors of TO Live
topics: decision-making;
brief: This is a procedural item: the TO Live Planning and Priorities Committee recommends that the Board of Directors outline the organization's 2021 goals and objectives and authorize public release of the confidential information in Appendices 1 through 6 once adopted, at the CEO's discretion.

title: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Committee
body: Board of Directors of TO Live
topics: governance; governance structure; municipal governance
brief: This is a procedural item: a TO Live board member proposes establishing an Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) committee of three to five members, with Myriam Gafarou agreeing to serve as chair. No formal recommendation beyond the proposal is attached.

title: Canadian Heritage Grant Application
body: Board of Directors of TO Live
topics: subsidies and grants; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: The President and CEO of TO Live asks the Board of Directors to authorize management to apply to the federal Department of Canadian Heritage's Canada Arts Presentation Fund for funding to present programming for TO Live's 2022 season at the Meridian Arts Centre.

title: President and Chief Executive Officer's General Status Update
body: Board of Directors of TO Live
topics: information;
brief: This is an information item: the President and CEO of TO Live gives the Board of Directors a general status update and a report on fourth-quarter 2020 activities at TO Live's three theatres: Meridian Hall, Meridian Arts Centre, and St. Lawrence Centre. The board is asked to receive the report for information. No decision is attached.

title: 2946-2968 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Final Report
topics: planning, rental housing, zoning; rental properties; rental units
brief: This is a final report on zoning by-law amendment and rental housing demolition applications for 2946-2968 Dundas Street West, which propose an 8-storey mixed-use building with 120 dwelling units including 8 rental replacement units, 1,973 square metres of retail, and 1,660 square metres of office space. The report finds the proposal consistent with provincial policy and recommends that City Council approve the zoning amendments to the former Toronto Zoning By-law 438-86 and City-wide By-law 569-2013.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 8D to exclude the development located at 1249-1251 Queen Street East
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to amend Schedule B of the Permit Parking by-law (Chapter 925) to realign Permit Parking Area 8D, excluding the development at 1249-1251 Queen Street East. The change would bar the General Manager from accepting on-street permit parking applications from residents, visitors, and tradespeople at that development.

title: Pay-and-Display Parking - Broadview Avenue, Danforth Avenue, Coxwell Avenue and Pape Avenue
topics: parking, parking machines; pay and display machines; pay-and-display machines
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to approve additional pay-and-display parking spaces on streets running off Danforth Avenue between Broadview Avenue and Dawes Road, to offset parking lost to the ActiveTO cycle tracks on Danforth, plus changes to the hours when paid parking applies on Danforth between Donlands and Woodbine. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Danforth Avenue.

title: Road Alteration and Parking Amendments - Queen Street West
topics: parking spaces, stopping prohibitions; no stopping, parking spots
brief: The Queen Street West BIA's second phase of its Streetscape Master Plan would create expanded public pedestrian space and public bike parking on Queen Street West, requiring permanent removal of two parking spaces and changes to stopping rules on the north side of Queen Street West between Bathurst Street and a point west of Bay Street. The work would be bundled with TTC and Toronto Water projects planned from Bay Street to Shaw Avenue.
address: Toronto Ontario Queen Bathurst; Toronto Ontario Queen Spadina

title: Construction Staging Area - 193-195 McCaul Street
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction, transportation; building, transportation services, ttc
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize construction staging for BJL McCaul Incorporated's 20-storey residential development at 193-195 McCaul Street, between Dundas Street West and College Street. The request covers closing the east sidewalk and a 1.8-metre-wide portion of the northbound curb lane on McCaul Street, between a point 71 metres north of Elm Street and a point 45 metres further north, from April 1, 2021 to February 29, 2024. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on McCaul Street.

title: Construction Staging Area Time Extension - 1 Bloor Street West, Phase 2 - (Yonge Street and Bloor Street West)
topics: construction, transportation; building, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize extending the construction staging closure for Mizrahi Developments' 86-storey residential tower with an eight-storey retail podium at 1 Bloor Street West. The request covers continuing the closure of the west sidewalk and a three-metre-wide portion of the southbound curb lane on Yonge Street, between Bloor Street West and a point 66 metres south, from September 1, 2020 to December 31, 2021. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Yonge Street and Bloor Street West.

title: 1- 7 Yonge Street - Public Art Plan
brief: Staff seek City Council approval of the public art plan for 1 Yonge Street, which outlines how the owner will commission public art beside the publicly owned corner plaza. The plan covers the project team, the Section 37 agreement, public art objectives, a mentorship opportunity, locations, budget, and the selection process and jury. The City Planning Division recommends Council approve the plan.

title: Application to Remove a Private Ravine Protected Tree - 17 Langmuir Crescent
topics: ravine protection, tree removal; ravine bylaws; ravine protection bylaws
brief: This report asks City Council to deny a permit to remove one privately owned ravine-protected black walnut tree at 17 Langmuir Crescent. The applicant says the tree drops large quantities of nuts, making the rear yard unusable. The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends denial because the 97-centimetre-diameter tree is healthy and maintainable under the Ravine and Natural Feature Protection By-law.

title: 10-30 Dawes Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Direction
topics: zoning;
brief: This is a request-for-direction report on a zoning by-law amendment application for 10-30 Dawes Road, which proposes two towers of 24 and 41 storeys on a shared base with 616 residential units plus retail, office, and daycare uses. The applicant appealed to the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal on November 6, 2020 after Council failed to decide within the Planning Act timeframe. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council authorize the City Solicitor and staff to attend the LPAT hearing in opposition to the application.
address: 10 Dawes Toronto Ontario; 30 Dawes Toronto Ontario

title: 1521 Queen Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Direction
topics: zoning;
brief: This is a request-for-direction report on a zoning by-law amendment application for 1521 Queen Street West, which proposed an 8-storey mixed-use building with 78 residential units and about 300 square metres of ground-floor retail. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the application in its current form at the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal hearing, and defer making a decision on the application.

title: Inclusion on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register- 55 Elm Street (650 Bay Street) and 57-71 Elm Street
topics: heritage properties, planning, urban design; civic improvements, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council include nine properties on Elm Street on the City's Heritage Register for their cultural heritage value: 55 Elm Street (entrance at 650 Bay Street) and 57 through 71 Elm Street, on the south side of Elm between Bay and Elizabeth streets. The group includes a 3-storey Renaissance Revival corner commercial building and five attached 2.5-storey Bay-n-Gable dwellings built in 1891.
address: 55-71 Elm Toronto Ontario; 650 Bay Toronto Ontario

title: Inclusion on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register- 22 Rose Park Drive
topics: heritage designation, planning;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council include 22 Rose Park Drive on the City's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value. The Moore Park property holds a two-storey stucco house built around 1909 in the Dutch Colonial Revival style, a rare example of the style in the neighbourhood and among its earliest houses.

title: Inclusion on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register- 103 Heath Street West
topics: heritage properties, planning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council include 103 Heath Street West on the City's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value. The property holds a 2.5-storey late Victorian red brick house built around 1892-1893, among the earliest houses on that section of Heath Street West and in the Deer Park neighbourhood.

title: Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property and Amendment of a Heritage Easement Agreement - 314 Jarvis Street
topics: heritage designation;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve alterations to the designated Dr. Charles Sheard House at 314 Jarvis Street and authorize amending the existing Heritage Easement Agreement. The house was extensively damaged by two fires; the remaining portions will be retained and the missing portions reconstructed, with a rear addition connecting it to a 34-storey mixed-use building with a 10-storey base fronting on the property.

title: Intention to Designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property, and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement - 938, 944, and 950 King Street West and 95, 97, and 99 Strachan Avenue
topics: heritage properties, planning, urban design; civic improvements, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the properties at 938, 944, and 950 King Street West and 95, 97, and 99 Strachan Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The properties include four semi-detached townhouses, a three-storey building, and three attached townhouses in the Queen Anne Revival and Richardsonian Romanesque styles, designed by architect Frederick Henry Herbert and built between 1889 and 1897.
address: 95-99 Strachan Toronto Ontario; 938-950 King Toronto Ontario

title: Permanent Closure of the City-owned Public Lane Known as Brigden Place
topics: full closures (traffic calming), transportation; transportation services
brief: Transportation Services recommends that City Council authorize the permanent closure of the City-owned public lane known as Brigden Place, west of Ontario Street and south of Queen Street East. Once closed, the lane would be sold to Richmond GP Inc., as general partner for Richmond Residential Limited Partnership, to be incorporated into the mixed-use redevelopment of the block bounded by Queen Street East, Ontario Street, Richmond Street East, and McFarrens Lane.

title: Inclusion on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register, Intention to Designate under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, Alterations to a Heritage Property and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement - 2946 Dundas Street West
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties, urban design; civic improvements, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council include 2946 Dundas Street West (with entrance addresses 2948, 2950, and 2952) on the City's Heritage Register, state its intention to designate the property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, approve the proposed alterations, and authorize a Heritage Easement Agreement. The 1921 William Rowntree Block in the Junction is a fine Neo-Gothic style building.

title: 536 and 538 Brunswick Avenue - Part-Lot Control Exemption Application - Final Report
topics: part lot control, planning;
brief: This is a final report on a part-lot control exemption application for 536 and 538 Brunswick Avenue, to create conveyable lots for six townhouses as Parcels of Tied Land to a common-elements condominium driveway, lifting part-lot control for two years subject to conditions. The owner would also register a Section 118 restriction under the Land Titles Act. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council enact the Part-Lot Control Exemption By-law.

title: 1245 Dupont Street and 1260 Dufferin Street - Draft Plan of Subdivision Application - Final Report
topics: applications, planning, subdivision (land); application process, subdivision of land
brief: This is a final report on a draft plan of subdivision application for 1245 Dupont Street and 1260 Dufferin Street, the Reimagine Galleria site, which proposes two new public streets, four new blocks for mixed-use development with privately owned publicly-accessible space, and one new block for part of a public park. The application follows the 2018 Council approval and incorporates City-owned lands occupied by the Wallace Emerson Community Centre. The Chief Planner intends to approve the draft plan under delegated authority.
address: 1260 Dufferin Toronto Ontario; 1245 Dupont Toronto Ontario

title: 968 O'Connor Drive  - Zoning Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: planning, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a final report on a zoning amendment application for 968 O'Connor Drive, at the northwest corner of O'Connor Drive and Curity Avenue, to permit a 10-storey mixed-use building on the currently vacant lot. The proposal includes 126 residential units, four two-storey townhouses, 383 square metres of ground-floor retail, 131 bicycle parking spaces, and indoor and outdoor amenity space. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council approve the amendments to the former East York Zoning By-law and City-wide Zoning By-law 569-2013.

title: 545 Commissioners Street - Site Plan Control Application and City-initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Final Report
topics: planning, site plan control; site plan approvals
brief: This is a final report on a site plan control application and City-initiated zoning by-law amendment for 545 Commissioners Street, which proposes a concrete batching and mixing yard, builder's supply yard, and open storage of raw materials, with office, retail, and vehicle repair uses as ancillary. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council approve the zoning amendments to By-law 438-86 and related by-laws.

title: 15 Delisle Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: Official Plans, zoning;
brief: This is a final report on an Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendment application for 15 Delisle Avenue, an intervening property between the approved 44-storey development at 1-11 Delisle Avenue and 1496-1510 Yonge Street and the new 2,506-square-metre off-site public park at the rear of 30 and 40 St. Clair Avenue West. The pre-conditions of the July 2020 Council approval have not yet been fulfilled and the bills have not been introduced; the applicant now seeks to add the intervening property. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council approve the amendments for 15 Delisle Avenue.
address: 1 Delisle Toronto Ontario; 15 Delisle Toronto Ontario; 1496 Yonge Toronto Ontario; 1510 Yonge Toronto Ontario

title: 364 Huron Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: official plan amendments, planning, zoning;
brief: This is a final report on an Official Plan and Zoning amendment application for 364 Huron Street, which proposes a three-storey mixed-use building with non-residential uses on the first two storeys, one dwelling unit on the third storey, and a two-storey laneway suite. The report finds the compact proposal consistent with provincial policy and the Official Plan, and recommends that City Council approve the amendments.

title: 938 - 950 King Street West and 95 - 99 Strachan Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a final report on a zoning by-law amendment application for 938-950 King Street West and 95-99 Strachan Avenue, which proposes a 14-storey mixed-use building with 191 residential units including up to 31 affordable units, 264 square metres of retail, 14 visitor parking spaces, and 202 bicycle parking spaces. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council approve the amendment to City-wide Zoning By-law 569-2013.

title: 663 King Street West, 69-73 Bathurst Street and 58-60 Stewart Street- Rental Housing Demolition Application - Final Report
topics: rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: This is a final report on a rental housing demolition application for 58-60 Stewart Street, which proposes demolishing seven existing rental units and replacing them as part of a larger development also subject to a zoning application appealed to the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal. A settlement offer was endorsed by City Council in January 2019, and Council deferred the demolition decision. The City Planning Division now recommends that City Council approve the demolition of the seven rental units under Chapter 667 of the Municipal Code and Section 111 of the City of Toronto Act.
address: 58 Stewart Toronto Ontario; 60 Stewart Toronto Ontario

title: Permanent Closure of a Portion of the Western Terminus of Randolph Avenue
topics: road closures; street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Transportation Services recommends that City Council authorize the permanent closure of a 4.5-square-metre portion of the western terminus of Randolph Avenue (Part 20 on Plan 66R-31423) and its sale to Metrolinx, in connection with the Kitchener Corridor GO Transit expansion, specifically the Bloor GO Station building pavilion.

title: Request for Directions Report - 2200 to 2206 Eglinton Avenue East, 1020 to 1030 Birchmount Road and 75 Thermos Road - Official Plan Amendment Application
topics: official plan amendments;
brief: This is a request-for-directions report on an Official Plan amendment application for 2200 to 2206 Eglinton Avenue East, 1020 to 1030 Birchmount Road, and 75 Thermos Road, within the Golden Mile Secondary Plan area, which seeks a Site and Area-Specific Policy to permit mixed-use redevelopment with new public streets and parkland. The applicant appealed to the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal after Council failed to decide within the Planning Act timeframe. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the appeal at the LPAT.
address: 1020-1030 Birchmount Toronto Ontario; 2200-2206 Eglinton Toronto Ontario; 75 Thermos Toronto Ontario

title: Request for Directions Report - 1920 to 1940 Eglinton Avenue East, 880 to 900 Warden Avenue and 20 to 50 Ashtonbee Road - Official Plan Amendment Application
brief: This is a request-for-directions report on an Official Plan amendment application for 1920 to 1940 Eglinton Avenue East, 880 to 900 Warden Avenue, and 20 to 50 Ashtonbee Road, within the Golden Mile Secondary Plan area, which seeks a Site and Area-Specific Policy to permit a mixed-use development with new public streets and parkland. The applicant appealed to the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal after Council failed to decide within the Planning Act timeframe. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the appeal at the LPAT.
address: 1920-1940 Eglingon Toronto Ontario; 20-50 Ashtonbee Toronto Ontario; 880-900 Warden Toronto Ontario

title: Request for Directions Report - 1900 Eglinton Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment Application
topics: official plan amendments;
brief: This is a request-for-directions report on an Official Plan amendment application for 1900 Eglinton Avenue East, within the Golden Mile Secondary Plan area, which seeks a Site and Area-Specific Policy to permit a mixed-use development with new public streets and parkland. The applicant appealed to the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal after Council failed to decide within the Planning Act timeframe. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the appeal at the LPAT.

title: Refusal Report 2872, 2880 and 2882 Kingston Road - Zoning Amendment Application
topics: rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a refusal report for a zoning amendment application for 2872, 2880, and 2882 Kingston Road, which proposes a 10-storey mixed-use building with 145 dwelling units and 295 square metres of ground-floor commercial space at a density of 4.99 times the lot area. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council refuse the application in its current form because the site is not appropriate for the size of the proposal, and authorize the City Solicitor to act on the refusal.
address: 2872 Kingston Toronto Ontario; 2880 Kingston Toronto Ontario; 2882 Kingston Toronto Ontario

title: U-Turn Prohibition - Kingston Road and Falaise Road
topics: turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to prohibit eastbound U-turns at all times on Kingston Road at Falaise Road, since the TTC operates transit service on Kingston Road. Prohibiting the U-turns would provide a safer environment for all road users at the intersection.

title: Final Report - 1050 Military Trail - Zoning Amendment Application
topics: rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a final report on a zoning amendment application for 1050 Military Trail on the University of Toronto Scarborough campus, seeking to remove a Holding provision to permit the five-storey, 14,930-square-metre Instructional Centre Phase 2 building with classrooms, lecture halls, offices, and some retail. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council approve the amendment to the Highland Creek Community Zoning By-law.

title: Housekeeping Amendments to Municipal Code Chapter 363 (Construction and Demolition By-law)

No change to the substance of demolition control is described.

title: 7080 Yonge Street in the City of Vaughan - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Request for Direction Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a request-for-direction report on applications in the City of Vaughan for 7080 Yonge Street, north of Steeles Avenue West, which propose two mixed-use towers with 652 residential units. The applications were circulated to Toronto because of the proximity to the city boundary. The Chief Planner recommends that City Council endorse staff's January 18, 2021 letter to Vaughan identifying concerns about height and density.

title: Temporary Use Zoning By-laws to Provide an Extension to Existing Temporary Permissions for Outdoor Patios for Bars and Restaurants
topics: boulevard cafes, zoning bylaws; boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants), zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Planning Division recommends that City Council extend the city-wide temporary use by-laws under Section 39 of the Planning Act that ease zoning restrictions on outdoor patios for bars, restaurants, take-out establishments, and recreation uses. The current by-laws expire May 25, 2021, and extending them would give patio operators certainty as they plan for the season, complementing the CaféTO program.

title: Extending the Toronto Community Housing Corporation (TCHC) Moratorium on Evictions due to Non-Payment of Rent
topics: eviction, payment, rent; paying; payment information; payment methods; payment options; pre-authorized payment plans; pre-authorized plans; preauthorized payments, rents
brief: The General Manager of Shelter, Support and Housing Administration recommends that, if the provincial eviction enforcement pause stops applying to Toronto, City Council ask the Toronto Community Housing Corporation board to continue its moratorium on evictions for non-payment of rent until June 17, 2021. City Council requested a three-month moratorium in December 2020, and the Province later paused enforcement of non-emergency evictions under its January 12, 2021 state of emergency.

title: Partnership with United Property Resource Corporation to Create 500 New Affordable Rental Homes
topics: affordable housing, partnerships; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: The Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat recommends that City Council authorize negotiating and entering into a Memorandum of Understanding with the United Property Resource Corporation to advance the land bank initiative under the HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan, which targets 40,000 new affordable rental homes by 2030. The partnership would help identify and set aside land for affordable housing.

title: Open Door Program 2020 Call for Applications Results: Supporting 971 New Affordable Rental Homes
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: The Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat recommends that City Council approve 15 affordable housing developments, representing 971 new affordable rental homes, from the 2020 Open Door Program call for applications. Eleven of the 15 are proposed by non-profit housing providers, including three Indigenous groups; the applications were assessed by an interdivisional staff committee after the September-to-November 2020 call.
