title: Creating Indigenous Supportive Housing at 218 Carlton Street
topics: First Nations, housing; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, homes; residences
brief: The Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat and the Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management recommend that City Council authorize the City to accept an offer to lease and enter into a 50-year lease for nominal consideration with Native Men's Residence for 218 Carlton Street. The non-profit Indigenous housing provider was selected through a December 2020 request for proposals to operate the property as affordable rental housing for Indigenous men.

title: Activating a Revitalization Plan for the Dundas Sherbourne Neighbourhood
topics: community development, redevelopment; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: The Executive Directors of the Housing Secretariat and Social Development, Finance and Administration recommend that City Council, as sole shareholder, direct the Toronto Community Housing Corporation board to have its CEO carry out next steps on the neighbourhood revitalization plan for the Dundas East and Sherbourne Street area, including work on the Dan Harrison Community Complex master plan. Council adopted the revitalization direction in December 2019 and asked staff to report back with a proposed plan.

title: Request to Province on Status and Timing of Funding Commitments for new schools in the Central Waterfront
topics: schools, waterfronts; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: Councillor Joe Cressy recommends that City Council ask the Minister of Education and the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing to identify the status and timing of provincial funding to build public elementary schools in Toronto's Central Waterfront. The waterfront's population grew 53 percent since 2016 to 39,000, with about 27,000 homes in the pipeline and a potential buildout population of 115,000, but the only public elementary school is the 250-student Waterfront School.

title: Update on Short-term Rental Regulations
topics: affordable housing, regulations, zoning bylaws; affordable homes; housing projects, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: at its February 2, 3, and 5, 2021 meeting, City Council referred the short-term rental regulations item back to the Planning and Housing Committee for further consideration. No decision is attached beyond the referral.

title: Modular Housing Initiative:  Phase Two Sites - 175 Cummer Avenue and Trenton/Cedarvale Avenue
topics: city initiatives, housing; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, homes; residences
brief: This report presents two sites for Phase Two of the City's Modular Housing Initiative: 175 Cummer Avenue in Willowdale and a lot at Trenton and Cedarvale avenues in Beaches-East York. It outlines the recommended planning approval process and community engagement, with community meetings proposed in March to present site and building designs for input. The Chief Planner and the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat recommend the Planning and Housing Committee direct staff to proceed with the approvals process.

title: Refusal Report - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - 36 to 44 Eglinton Avenue West
topics: redevelopment, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: This is a refusal report for a zoning by-law amendment application for 36 to 44 Eglinton Avenue West, which proposes a 65-storey mixed-use building with 663 dwelling units and 550 square metres of retail and office space, at 45,112 square metres of gross floor area and a density of 32.27 times the lot area. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council refuse the application for the reasons in the February 4, 2021 report and authorize the City Solicitor to act on the refusal.

title: Request for Direction Report - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - 5995 to 5997 Yonge Street
topics: redevelopment, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: This is a request-for-direction report on a zoning by-law amendment application for 5995 to 5997 Yonge Street, which proposes a 40-storey mixed-use building with 443 residential units. The applicant appealed to the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal after Council failed to decide within the Planning Act timeframe, with a hearing scheduled to begin May 11, 2021. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the application at the LPAT hearing.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2527, 238 to 258 Finch Avenue East - North 88 Developments Inc.
topics: assumption of services, municipal services; city services
brief: This report recommends that City Council assume the municipal services installed under the subdivision agreement between North 88 Developments Inc. and the City for Plan 66M-2527, dated June 17, 2015. That means the City formally takes over the road and public lane within Kenneth Wood Crescent and Munshaw Lane, plus the stormwater drainage system within a municipal service easement.

title: Inclusion on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register - 19 Plymbridge Crescent
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council include 19 Plymbridge Crescent on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value. The Hogg's Hollow property holds a two-storey Tudor Revival house built around 1912 as stables, a rare converted-stables example and a remnant of the former Boultbee family estate, "The Hollow."

title: Proposed Speed Rate Reductions on Lawrence Avenue East and York Mills Road
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council previously referred a recommendation to reduce the speed limit from 60 km/h to 50 km/h on Lawrence Avenue East between Don Mills Road and Woodcliff Place and on York Mills Road between Bayview Avenue and Don Mills Road to the North York Community Council for consideration. No recommendation is attached beyond the referral.

title: Application to Remove a Private Tree - 147 Fenn Avenue
topics: privately-owned trees, tree removal; private owned trees; private trees; privately owned trees; trees on private property
brief: This report asks City Council to deny a permit to remove one privately owned honey locust tree at 147 Fenn Avenue. The applicant says the tree is too close to the dwelling, may affect the foundation, and its roots are heaving the interlocking walkway, creating an accessibility issue. The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends denial because the 64-centimetre-diameter tree is healthy and maintainable under the Private Tree By-law.

title: Request for Direction Report - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - 241 Redpath Avenue
topics: demolitions, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a request-for-direction report on zoning by-law amendment and rental housing demolition applications for 241 Redpath Avenue, which propose a 35-storey residential building on a 7- and 11-storey base at an FSI of 15.77, including demolishing 46 existing rental units that would be replaced in the new development. The applicant appealed to the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal on November 6, 2020. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the applications in their current form at the LPAT.

title: Lane Designation - One Way Traffic Lane Northbound Right Turn (Buses Excepted) - Bathurst Street and Finch Avenue West
topics: traffic direction; one way operations; one way streets; one way traffic; two way operations; two way streets; two way traffic
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to designate the northbound curb lane on Bathurst Street at Finch Avenue West as "right turn only, buses excepted," between Finch Avenue West and a point 45 metres south. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Bathurst Street; the designation would let TTC buses legally use the lane for pick-ups and drop-offs before merging back into traffic.

title: Request for Direction Report - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - 4050 Yonge Street
topics: official plan amendments, redevelopment, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: This is a request-for-direction report on Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendment applications for 4050 Yonge Street, which propose redeveloping a commercial parking lot into a 21-storey building with 29 residential units plus office, retail, restaurant, and hotel uses on the east portion, and a 35-storey, 271-unit residential building on the west portion, connected by a 6-storey base with access to the York Mills TTC/GO station. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the appeal at the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal hearing.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 751 King Street West for streetscape improvements in the Ossington Business Improvement Area - by Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
brief: Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, recommends that City Council release $50,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 751 King Street West to the Ossington Business Improvement Area for public art and streetscape improvements. The BIA has worked with the City on the renewal project for years and will maintain the improvements; the plan includes two parkettes that widen pedestrian clearways.

title: 2100-2110 Yonge Street and 8-12 Manor Road West- Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Supplementary Report - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends that City Council correct its October 2020 approval for the 12-storey mixed-use redevelopment of 2100-2110 Yonge Street, which secured replacement of 7 rental units. After approval, staff discovered the report had misidentified the rental units; the motion replaces recommendations 7.b and 7.c with corrected ones from the Chief Planner's March 1, 2021 report.

title: Supporting Canadian News Media - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: mass media; broadcast media; media organizations; print media; web media
brief: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, recommends that City Council declare a healthy professional news media essential to democracy and urge municipal councils across Canada to do the same. The motion notes outlets closing and thousands of jobs lost as traditional revenue streams decline, and the federal financial assistance made available in response.

title: Heritage Plaque to Commemorate the Elihu Pease House at 20 Harrison Garden Boulevard funded by Section 45(9) Planning Act Reserve Funds - by Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: historic sites; heritage buildings; heritage sites; historical sites
brief: Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends that City Council release $1,625 in Section 45 funds to Heritage Toronto for a heritage plaque commemorating the Elihu Pease house at 20 Harrison Garden Boulevard. Built in 1834, it is one of the oldest surviving homes in North York; the funds come from community benefits from the development at 4726-4728 Yonge Street.

title: 1169 St. Clair Avenue West - Liquor Licence Application - 7-Eleven - File 1091284 - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends that City Council oppose the liquor licence application for the 7-Eleven at 1169 St. Clair Avenue West, which lacks community support and is considered not in the community interest. Council is asked to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that issuing the licence is not in the public interest.

title: 1260 Dundas Street West - Liquor Licence Application - 7-Eleven - File 1091272 - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends that City Council oppose the liquor licence application for the 7-Eleven at 1260 Dundas Street West, which lacks community support and is considered not in the community interest. Council is asked to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that issuing the licence is not in the public interest.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 (Planning Act) Funds from various developments for capital improvements to the future space of the Indigenous Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship at 200 Dundas Street East - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: cultural facilities, funding; art centres; arts centres; cultural attractions; cultural centres, financing
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, recommends that City Council release $4,069,421.64 in Section 37 funds for capital improvements to the future home of the Indigenous Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship at 200 Dundas Street East. The 22,000-square-foot City-owned space would house a non-profit organization; the motion also increases the project's capital budget from $3,783,816.13 to cover the work.

title: Proclaiming Bangladeshi Heritage Month and Independence Day of Bangladesh - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: congratulatory messages; letter of greeting; proclamations; scrolls
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, recommends that City Council proclaim March as Bangladeshi Heritage Month and March 26 as Independence Day of Bangladesh each year. Toronto is home to a large Bangladeshi community, and March 26 marks the 1971 independence of Bangladesh from Pakistan.

title: Protecting Residents and Businesses During the Broadview Watermain and Toronto Transit Commission Construction - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction, watermain connections; building, lead pipes; lead service pipe replacement; water service connections; water service repair programs; wsr, ttc
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council direct the Chief Engineer to add requirements to the tender for the Broadview watermain and TTC track replacement projects, between Gerrard Street East and Danforth Avenue, to protect residents and businesses during construction. The two projects, scheduled for 2021 and 2022, will disrupt an area already strained by other construction and the pandemic.

title: Requesting the Deferral of Development Charges for Anishnawbe Health Toronto at 425 Cherry Street East - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: health; health coverage
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council ask the Chief Financial Officer, City Solicitor, and Chief Building Official to report to the April 7-8, 2021 Council meeting on whether development charges can be deferred for Anishnawbe Health Toronto's new site at 425 Cherry Street East. The Indigenous community health centre has served Toronto since 1989 and provides primary care similar to a public hospital.

title: Feasibility Study - Repurpose Toronto Parking Authority Green P Lot at 20 Shortt Street for a Community Service Hub and Affordable Housing Development - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: parking;
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, recommends that City Council ask the Chief Planner, with Parks, Forestry and Recreation, the Toronto Parking Authority, Social Development, and CreateTO, to study repurposing the Green P lot at 20 Shortt Street for a community service hub and affordable housing. The Eglinton Avenue West corridor is seeing heavy development without enough social and recreational infrastructure to support new residents.

title: 0 Skeens Lane - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Michael Ford
topics: appeals, applications, committees of adjustment, council meetings, councillors, neighbourhoods, planning tribunals; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council, application process, committee of adjustment, cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods, omb; ontario municipal board
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Michael Ford, recommends that City Council authorize the City Solicitor and staff to oppose, at the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal, a variance to add nine visitor parking spaces on a separate lot at 0 Skeens Lane for the 5-storey condo at 3418 Lake Shore Boulevard West. The Skeens Lane property is designated Neighbourhoods in the Official Plan, unlike the mixed-use condo site.

title: Cannabis Retail Locations - Protecting  Youth and Communities - by Councillor Cynthia Lai, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: liquor sales licences, stores; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, retail stores; shops
brief: Councillor Cynthia Lai, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas, recommends that City Council ask the Ontario government and the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario not to approve cannabis retail stores inside shopping centres or malls. Nine applications have come in for Scarborough North alone, and malls like Splendid China Mall are places where youth congregate.

title: Google MisGeography: Clarifying the pre-amalgamation boundaries for Parks, Forestry and Recreation and all other City Divisions - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: maps;
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, recommends that City Council direct the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to review how park districts are designated so the former Borough of East York is recognized as distinct from the other legacy municipalities, and direct other divisions to use the pre-amalgamation boundaries correctly. East York residents noticed parks across Toronto, including in the West Don Lands, being listed as in East York.

title: Accelerating the Affordable Housing and Cultural Animation Opportunities at 15 Dension Avenue - by Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, recommends that City Council direct the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat, with CreateTO and Economic Development and Culture, to accelerate plans to redevelop 15 Denison Avenue for affordable housing and cultural uses. Council first asked staff to explore the site in July 2018 and again directed work on the property in December 2020, with consideration of a non-profit development partner.

title: 2010-2016 Bathurst Street - Technical Amendment to Zoning By-law - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends that City Council correct four omissions in the site-specific zoning by-laws for the approved 8-storey, 26-unit residential building at 2010-2016 Bathurst Street: the mechanical penthouse storey label, the first-floor setback, the varied first-floor height, and building projections. Staff recommend the technical amendments to match the architectural plans.

title: Support for New Non-Profit Affordable Housing on City Lands at 25 Bellevue Avenue - Section 37 Funds for Pre-Development Work - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council authorize up to $150,000 in Section 37 funds from Ward 11 developments for due diligence and pre-development work on the Toronto Parking Authority lot at 25 Bellevue Avenue in Kensington Market. Council designated the lot for non-profit affordable rental housing in July 2020, and the funds would pay for environmental and engineering studies ahead of a competitive call for a non-profit developer.

title: Authorization to enter into a Construction and License Agreement with the Friends of University Avenue for a Lighting Enhancement Project in University Median Park - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: agreements, construction, council meetings, councillors, improvement, landscaping, licences, projects, street lighting; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council, building, enhancement; rehabilitation (property), landscapers, licenses; licensing, tenancy agreements
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, recommends that City Council oppose the Province's proposed Greater Toronto Area West Highway (Highway 413), a 400-series highway in the northwest GTA. The motion says the highway threatens farmland, waterways, Greenbelt lands, and conservation areas, and that agriculture in the Greater Golden Horseshoe contributes $11 billion and 38,000 jobs to Ontario's economy.

title: Improving Living Conditions for Tenants at 138 Pears Avenue during COVID-19 - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: tenants; renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council transfer $229,208.45 to the Housing Secretariat's 2021 operating budget, on a one-time basis, to fund St. Clare's Multifaith Housing Society's modernization of the affordable rental units at 138 Pears Avenue, adding kitchens inside the units. The funding would come from Section 37 community benefits from the development at 250 Davenport Road.

title: Supporting the Greenbelt and Opposing Highway 413 - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: highways, provincial highways; freeways; motorways; parkways
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, recommends that City Council authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to negotiate and execute a construction and licence agreement with the Friends of University Avenue for a lighting enhancement project in University Median Park. The citizen-led non-profit proposed temporary lighting and landscaping to lift the spirits of patients in nearby hospitals; Council supported the proposal in September 2020.

title: Exploring Round the Clock Vaccination - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: disease outbreaks; epidemics; pandemics
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends that City Council ask the Medical Officer of Health, with the Fire Chief and emergency management, to develop a plan for 24/7 vaccinations at City-run immunization clinics during Phase 3 of the provincial vaccine rollout. The motion argues round-the-clock hours would make vaccination more accessible and equitable as daily capacity ramps up.

title: Co-ordination of Capital Projects on Wellington Street West and Draper Street - by Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: development; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, recommends that City Council direct the Deputy City Manager to coordinate construction projects around Wellington Street West and Draper Street in the fast-growing King-Spadina area, whose population rose from 945 in 1996 to about 22,000 in 2018. The coordination covers the north boulevard of Wellington Street West between Spadina Avenue and Portland Street and other nearby work.

title: Request to Amend the 2021 Parks Forestry and Recreation Capital Budget for the Colonel Samuel Smith Park Cenotaph Improvements Project - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: improvement, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday, recommends that City Council amend the 2021-2030 Parks, Forestry and Recreation capital plan to create a new $292,000 sub-project for improvements to the Eighth Street Cenotaph in its new home at Colonel Samuel Smith Park. The improvements would add a gathering space, connecting pathway, lighting, and landscaping.

title: Supporting the Opportunity for a Post-Secondary Institution in Mount Dennis - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, council meetings, economic development, light rail transit, local government structure, post-secondary education, public transit; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, city council structure; committee structure; council committee structure; council structure; council-committee structure; governance structure, college education; graduate studies; higher education; post-graduate studies; postgraduate studies; postsecondary education; university applications; university education, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, lrt, ttc
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, recommends that City Council direct CreateTO, with Corporate Real Estate Management and Economic Development and Culture, to identify City-owned, other public, and private land in Mount Dennis for a potential post-secondary institution. Mount Dennis Station will soon be one of the City's largest transit hubs, connecting the Eglinton Crosstown, TTC buses, UP Express, and GO Transit.

title: Calling on the Provincial and Federal Governments to review the licences and approvals for the meat processing facility at 70 Glen Scarlett Road - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: business licences; business licensing; business permits; municipal licenses
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, recommends that City Council ask the Province and the federal government to review all licences and approvals for the meat processing facility at 70 Glen Scarlett Road. The former Ryding Regency plant has drawn complaints from Stockyards-area residents and businesses about noise, odour, and truck traffic.

title: Request to Demolish Non-Residential Building at 911X Castlefield Avenue - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends that City Council amend its July 2020 decision on the non-residential building demolition at 911X Castlefield Avenue: correct the address from "911X Castlefield Drive" to "911X Castlefield Avenue" and delete the condition requiring the owner to register the beautification agreement on title, since the owner has already satisfied the City Solicitor with its beautification plan.

title: 1390 Weston Road - Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario Liquor Licence Application - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: liquor sales licences, motions; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, council decisions; decisions (council)
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, recommends that City Council oppose the liquor licence application for the 7-Eleven at 1390 Weston Road, an indoor-area-only application near residential units where the community worries about noise and disturbance. Council is asked to tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario the licence is not in the public interest unless conditions are attached.

title: 25 Mabelle Avenue - Zoning By-Law Amendment Application - Request for Direction Report
topics: zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a request-for-direction report on a zoning by-law amendment application for 25 Mabelle Avenue, which the owner appealed to the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal on March 9, 2020 after Council failed to decide within the Planning Act timeframe; a 10-day hearing is scheduled starting April 19, 2021. The site holds a 30-storey rental apartment building with 416 units, with an open area on the west portion. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the application as proposed at the LPAT hearing.

title: 2839 Jane Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a final report on a zoning by-law amendment application for 2839 Jane Street, which proposes a 13-storey mixed-use building with 9 ground-floor commercial units and 190 residential units, at 42.2 metres including the mechanical penthouse and an FSI of 3.83. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council approve the amendments to the former North York Zoning By-law 7625 and City-wide By-law 569-2013.

title: Heavy Vehicles Prohibition - Bloor Street West between Aukland Road and a point 210.8 metres west of Markland Drive
topics: heavy truck prohibitions;
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to extend the existing heavy-vehicle prohibition on Bloor Street West so it runs from Aukland Road to a point 210.8 metres west of Markland Drive, rather than starting at Jopling Avenue. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on this section of Bloor Street West.

title: All-Way Stop Control - Hullmar Drive and Hisey Crescent - Northeast Intersection
topics: traffic signs; traffic regulatory signs
brief: Transportation Services recommends that City Council not authorize all-way stop control at the northeast intersection of Hullmar Drive and Hisey Crescent, because the assessment found the warrant criteria were not met. City Council approval would have been required because the TTC operates bus service on Hullmar Drive.

title: Traffic Control Signals and Traffic Amendments - Burnhamthorpe Road, between Dundas Street West and Kipling Avenue
topics: traffic control systems; traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize installing traffic control signals at the intersection of Burnhamthorpe Road and Burnhamthorpe Park Boulevard/Holloway Road. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates bus service on Burnhamthorpe Road; staff could not collect typical traffic data during the COVID-19 lockdown but are proceeding with the signals to improve safety.

title: Traffic Control Signals - Islington Avenue and Barker Avenue
topics: traffic control systems; traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize installing traffic control signals at the intersection of Islington Avenue and Barker Avenue. topics: disease outbreaks, licences; epidemics; pandemics, licenses; licensing
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends that City Council ask the federal government to invoke compulsory licensing laws to authorize generic copies of the COVID-19 vaccines and boost domestic production. Vaccine delivery delays from Pfizer and Moderna threaten the recovery, and the motion argues Ottawa has not done enough to encourage domestic manufacturing.

brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, recommends that City Council ask the City Manager to report to the June 1, 2021 Executive Committee on Scarborough transit options, including a technical assessment of moving ahead with the Scarborough Light Rail Transit. The TTC says the Scarborough RT will stop running after 2023, three years sooner than Council was told, adding an estimated 18 minutes to average commutes and over $300 million in costs.

Detailed design revealed thermal performance issues under the Toronto Green Standards, and the variance relief from the former North York Zoning By-law 7625 would address the building envelope.

title: 2165 Gerrard Street East - Appeal  to the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão

Planning staff consider the application supportable.

title: Business Licenses and COVID-19 Related Closures - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: business licences; business licensing; business permits; municipal licenses

title: Calling on the Province to Phase-Out Gas-Fired Electricity Generation - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: electricity; electric power; electricity usage
brief: Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, recommends that City Council ask the Ontario government to develop and implement a plan to phase out all gas-fired electricity generation as soon as possible, joining 13 other Ontario municipalities. The motion notes Toronto's 2019 commitment to net zero emissions by 2050 and the Province's plan to rely more on gas power as the Pickering Nuclear Station's licence expires at the end of 2024.

title: Cancelling City of Toronto Advertisement in Corriere Canadese - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: advertising;
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, recommends that City Council direct the City Manager to immediately stop all City paid advertising in Corriere Canadese.
